sentences.zh: 岳薦張廒黃學硃吳伯宗錢天潤蕭良昌李九

translations.literal: Yue Jian, Zhang Ao, Huang Xuezhu, Wu Bozong, Qian Tianrun, Xiao Liangchang, Li Jiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Jian, Zhang Ao, Huang Xuezhu, Wu Bozong, Qian Tianrun, Xiao Liangchang, and Li Jiu.

sentences.zh: 張某程含光陳福譙衿黃成富李長茂任天篤

translations.literal: Zhang Mou, Cheng Hanguang, Chen Fu, Qiao Jin, Huang Chengfu, Li Changmao, Ren Tiandu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mou, Cheng Hanguang, Chen Fu, Qiao Jin, Huang Chengfu, Li Changmao, and Ren Tiandu.

sentences.zh: 趙一桂黃調鼎楊藝咸默李晉福胡端友硃永慶王某

translations.literal: Zhao Yigui, Huang Diaoding, Yang Yi, Xian Mo, Li Jinfu, Hu Duanyou, Zhu Yongqing, Wang Mou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yigui, Huang Diaoding, Yang Yi, Xian Mo, Li Jinfu, Hu Duanyou, Zhu Yongqing, and Wang Mou.

sentences.zh: 張瑛郭氏僕胡穆孟苑亮楊越子賓吳鴻錫

translations.literal: Zhang Ying, Guo's servant, Hu Mumu, Yuan Liang, Yang Yue, Zi Bin, Wu Hongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying, a servant of the Guo family, Hu Mumu, Yuan Liang, Yang Yue, Zi Bin, and Wu Hongxi.

sentences.zh: 韓瑜程增李應卜塞勒王聯黎侗李秉道趙瓏

translations.literal: Han Yu, Cheng Zeng, Li Yingbu, Saile, Wang Lian, Li Tong, Li Bingdao, Zhao Long.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, Cheng Zeng, Li Yingbu, Saile, Wang Lian, Li Tong, Li Bingdao, and Zhao Long.

sentences.zh: 蔣堅李林孫高大鎬許所望邢清源王元鳳瑞

translations.literal: Jiang Jian, Li Linsun, Gao Dabao, Xu Suowang, Xing Qingyuan, Wang Yuan, Feng Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jian, Li Linsun, Gao Dabao, Xu Suowang, Xing Qingyuan, Wang Yuan, and Feng Rui.

sentences.zh: 方元衡葉成忠楊斯盛武訓呂聯珠

translations.literal: Fang Yuanheng, Ye Chengzhong, Yang Sisheng, Wu Xun, Lü Lianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yuanheng, Ye Chengzhong, Yang Sisheng, Wu Xun, and Lü Lianzhu.

sentences.zh: 岳薦，江南山陽人。

translations.literal: Yue Jian was a native of Shanyang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Jian was from Shanyang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 明末為諸生。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming he was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming he held licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 事父母謹，居喪哭踴，氣息僅屬，乃病羸終其身。

translations.literal: He served his parents with care; in mourning he wept and stamped until his breath barely remained, and thereafter he was frail and sickly for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He tended his parents with scrupulous devotion. During mourning he wept and stamped in grief until he was barely breathing, and from then on he remained frail and ill for the rest of his days.

sentences.zh: 庶弟甫生而其母暴疾死，薦亦生女，乃令妻棄女而乳其弟。

translations.literal: A younger brother by a concubine had just been born when their mother died suddenly of illness; Jian also had a daughter born, and he had his wife abandon the daughter and nurse the younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: When a younger half-brother had just been born, their mother died suddenly. Jian's wife had also given birth to a daughter, but he had her set the infant aside and nurse the boy instead.

sentences.zh: 弟病瘍，日夜啼，夫婦迭拊之，遂俱生瘍，血淋漓被體，不以為苦。

translations.literal: The younger brother had ulcerous sores and cried day and night; husband and wife took turns soothing him, and they too developed sores, blood streaming over their bodies, yet they did not regard it as suffering.
translations.idiomatic: The boy developed ulcerous sores and cried day and night. Husband and wife took turns holding him, and they too broke out in sores until blood ran over their bodies—yet they never counted it hardship.

sentences.zh: 張廒，陝西盩厔人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ao was a native of Zhouzhi in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ao was from Zhouzhi in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治初，山賊破其堡，殺廒兄廠，並掠廠子去。

translations.literal: Early in the Shunzhi reign, mountain bandits stormed their fort, killed Ao's elder brother Chang, and carried off Chang's son as well.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi era, mountain bandits overran their fort, killed Ao's elder brother Chang, and abducted Chang's son.

sentences.zh: 廒愍廠死且無後，負其子入山易廠子歸。

translations.literal: Ao pitied Chang for dying without an heir; carrying his own son on his back, he went into the mountains and exchanged him to bring Chang's son back.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving that Chang had died without an heir, Ao carried his own infant son into the hills and traded the boy to ransom his nephew.

sentences.zh: 方謀贖子，山賊引去，其子幼不能從，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Just as he was planning to redeem his son, the bandits led the boy away; because the child was too young to keep up, they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: While he was still plotting to recover his son, the bandits marched the boy off. Too young to keep pace, the child was killed.

sentences.zh: 廒復生子，與廠子並成立。

translations.literal: Ao later had another son, and both he and Chang's son grew to adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: Ao later fathered another son, and both boys grew to maturity.

sentences.zh: 黃學硃，福建甌寧人。

translations.literal: Huang Xuezhu was a native of Ouning in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xuezhu was from Ouning in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He held licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 順治間，縣有土寇，執學硃及其弟。

translations.literal: During the Shunzhi period there were local bandits in the county; they seized Xuezhu and his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shunzhi years local bandits seized Xuezhu and his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 度不能兩全，乃紿賊曰：「家有薄產，釋弟歸鬻產，以其值贖我，何如？」

translations.literal: Judging that both could not be saved, he deceived the bandits, saying: "Our family has a small estate. Release my brother to go sell it and use the proceeds to ransom me—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that both brothers could not survive, he tricked the bandits: "We have a modest property at home. Let my brother go sell it and ransom me with the proceeds—what do you say?"

sentences.zh: 賊疑，欲遣學硃，學硃曰：「我秀才，質重於弟。」

translations.literal: The bandits were suspicious and wished to send Xuezhu instead; Xuezhu said: "I am a licentiate; as a hostage I am worth more than my brother."
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were wary and meant to send Xuezhu home instead, but he said, "I am a licentiate—my life is worth more than my brother's as a hostage."

sentences.zh: 賊遂釋弟歸。

translations.literal: The bandits then released the younger brother to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits released the younger brother.

sentences.zh: 實無產，贖不至，學硃遂被戕。

translations.literal: In truth there was no estate, and no ransom came; Xuezhu was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: There was in fact no property, and no ransom ever arrived. Xuezhu was slain.

sentences.zh: 吳伯宗，山西稷山人。

translations.literal: Wu Bozong was a native of Jishan in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Bozong was from Jishan in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 早喪父母，二弟幼，與相依。

translations.literal: He lost his parents early; his two younger brothers were small and depended on him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he raised his two little brothers, who relied on him entirely.

sentences.zh: 居數年，先後皆失之。

translations.literal: After several years living together, he lost them both in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years both brothers were lost to him.

sentences.zh: 伯宗求弟遍遠近，久之，得季弟京師，為高氏僕。

translations.literal: Bozong searched for his brothers far and near; after a long time he found his youngest brother in the capital, serving the Gao household.
translations.idiomatic: Bozong searched near and far. Long afterward he traced his youngest brother to the capital, where the boy was a servant in the Gao household.

sentences.zh: 高氏遇之厚，曰：「吾為子善撫，子求得仲弟，與之俱歸。」

translations.literal: The Gaos treated him generously and said: "I will care for you well. When you find your middle brother, bring him home together."
translations.idiomatic: The Gaos treated him kindly and said, "I will look after you. When you find your middle brother, bring him home with you."

sentences.zh: 又久之，伯宗得仲弟消息，在寧古塔，乃躬往踪蹟之。

translations.literal: After still more time Bozong learned that his middle brother was at Ningguta; he went in person to track him down.
translations.idiomatic: Much later he learned his middle brother was at Ningguta and set out himself to find him.

sentences.zh: 仲弟屬將軍部，投牒訟焉。

translations.literal: The middle brother belonged to the general's headquarters; Bozong filed a petition to sue on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The middle brother was held under the general's command, and Bozong filed a formal complaint.

sentences.zh: 庭質，辭未畢，伯宗忽躍起，主者怒，撲之，血被面。

translations.literal: At the hearing, before he had finished speaking, Bozong suddenly leaped up; the presiding official was enraged and had him beaten until blood covered his face.
translations.idiomatic: At the hearing, before he could finish, Bozong sprang up. The magistrate flew into a rage and had him beaten until his face ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 伯宗徐曰：「民非敢與抗，適見略吾弟者，奴吾弟者，皆法所不宥，顧美衣帽，平立官側。

translations.literal: Bozong said calmly: "This subject does not dare resist authority. I have just seen those who robbed my brother and those who enslaved him—acts the law does not forgive—yet they stand in fine hats and robes, level with the officials at your side.
translations.idiomatic: Bozong said evenly, "I do not defy the court. But the men who robbed my brother and made him a slave—crimes the law forbids—stand there in fine dress, shoulder to shoulder with your officers.

sentences.zh: 民兄弟良家子，為奸人誘掠，萬里投命，官不明其冤，乃視若罪囚，使跪而聽命，民是以不服。」

translations.literal: We brothers are sons of respectable families, lured and seized by villains and cast a thousand li from home to beg justice. The court does not see our wrong, yet treats us like convicts, making us kneel and obey—that is why this subject will not submit."
translations.idiomatic: We are men of good families, snatched by rogues and dragged ten thousand li from home. You will not hear our grievance, yet treat us like criminals on their knees—that is why I will not bow to this."

sentences.zh: 主者悟，白將軍，歸其仲弟。

translations.literal: The presiding official understood, reported to the general, and returned his middle brother to him.
translations.idiomatic: The official took his meaning, reported to the general, and restored the middle brother.

sentences.zh: 時正冬，兄弟相扶行冰雪中，至京師，與季弟同歸。

translations.literal: It was deep winter; the brothers supported each other through ice and snow to the capital and returned home together with the youngest brother.
translations.idiomatic: It was midwinter. The brothers helped each other through ice and snow to the capital and went home with the youngest at last.

sentences.zh: 錢天潤，江蘇宜興人。

translations.literal: Qian Tianrun was a native of Yixing in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Tianrun was from Yixing in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 少孤，為人傭耕，得錢必奉母。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he hired himself out to farm; whatever money he earned he gave to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he hired out as a farm laborer and gave every coin he earned to his mother.

sentences.zh: 母死，以奉其兄。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he used his earnings to support his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, he devoted his earnings to his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 有女弟嫁而寡，甥二，方幼，天潤往視之。

translations.literal: He had a married younger sister who was widowed, with two young nephews; Tianrun went to visit them.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sister had married and been widowed, leaving two small nephews; Tianrun went to see them.

sentences.zh: 女弟泣言：「夫死子幼，不知所以為計。」

translations.literal: His sister wept and said: "My husband is dead and my sons are young; I do not know what to do."
translations.idiomatic: His sister wept, "My husband is dead and my boys are small—I do not know how we shall live."

sentences.zh: 天潤問其意，女弟言：「原守節，第苦貧。」

translations.literal: Tianrun asked her mind; his sister said: "I wish to remain chaste, only poverty is hard."
translations.idiomatic: He asked what she wanted. She said, "I mean to keep my widowhood—only poverty stands in the way."

sentences.zh: 天潤曰：「妹無憂！

translations.literal: Tianrun said: "Sister, do not worry!
translations.idiomatic: "Do not fret, sister!

sentences.zh: 吾助汝。」

translations.literal: I will help you."
translations.idiomatic: I will see to it."

sentences.zh: 遂為女弟耕以給食。

translations.literal: He then farmed for his sister to provide food.
translations.idiomatic: He tilled fields for her and kept the household fed.

sentences.zh: 三年，女弟死，撫二甥，畢姻娶。

translations.literal: After three years his sister died; he raised the two nephews and saw them married.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later his sister died. He raised both nephews and saw them wed.

sentences.zh: 蕭良昌，湖南邵陽人。

translations.literal: Xiao Liangchang was a native of Shaoyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Liangchang was from Shaoyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 家貧，貿漆，事父孝。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he traded in lacquer and served his father filially.
translations.idiomatic: Poor as he was, he dealt in lacquer and served his father with exemplary devotion.

sentences.zh: 兄弟四，良昌其少季。

translations.literal: There were four brothers; Liangchang was the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: He was the youngest of four brothers.

sentences.zh: 析居，伯、仲、叔皆有一子，伯、仲早卒，叔攜其子出遊，良昌召伯、仲子與同居，率之貿荊、襄間。

translations.literal: When the household divided, the eldest, second, and third brothers each had one son; the eldest and second died early, and the third took his son traveling. Liangchang summoned the sons of the eldest and second to live with him and led them trading between Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: After the family split up, each elder brother had one son. The eldest and second died young; the third left on a long journey with his boy. Liangchang took in his elder brothers' orphans and led them trading between Jingzhou and Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 家漸起，始娶婦。

translations.literal: The family gradually prospered, and he then took a wife.
translations.idiomatic: The household slowly prospered, and only then did he marry.

sentences.zh: 歲除，具酒奉父，父語良昌曰：「兒能撫存孤侄甚善，顧安得汝叔兄父子復還耶？」

translations.literal: At year's end he set out wine for his father; his father said to Liangchang: "You have done well to nurture the orphaned nephews, but how can your uncle and cousin ever return?"
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve he served his father wine. The old man said, "You have done well by your orphaned nephews—but when will your uncle and cousin come home?"

sentences.zh: 良昌跪白父曰；

translations.literal: Liangchang knelt and told his father:
translations.idiomatic: Liangchang knelt and said,

sentences.zh: 「兒欲行求久矣。」

translations.literal: "I have long wished to go search for them."
translations.idiomatic: "I have wanted to go look for them for a long time."

sentences.zh: 明歲遂行。

translations.literal: The next year he set out.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he set out.

sentences.zh: 時傳叔兄在雲南，良昌行六閱月，貲且盡，途窮哭泣，目盡腫。

translations.literal: Word had it that his uncle and cousin were in Yunnan. Liangchang traveled six months until his funds were nearly gone; destitute on the road, he wept until his eyes swelled shut.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor placed his uncle and cousin in Yunnan. After six months on the road his money was gone; broke and weeping, his eyes swelled shut.

sentences.zh: 晨行至一村，遇曉汲者，則叔兄子也，乃與見叔兄，偕歸，父乃大慰。

translations.literal: One morning he reached a village and met someone drawing water at dawn—it was his uncle's son. He was reunited with uncle and cousin and brought them home; his father was greatly comforted.
translations.idiomatic: One dawn he came to a village and met a boy drawing water—it was his cousin. He found uncle and cousin, brought them home, and his father was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘，乃為諸子析居，厚兄子而薄其子，其子亦受之無間言。

translations.literal: When he was over eighty he divided the estate among his sons, favoring his brothers' sons over his own; his sons accepted it without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Past eighty he divided property among his sons, giving more to his nephews than to his own boys, who accepted the arrangement without a murmur.

sentences.zh: 李九，江蘇贛榆人。

translations.literal: Li Jiu was a native of Ganyu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiu was from Ganyu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 家青口，兄七，與其鄰爭地而訟，知縣吳元納鄰賕，逮七，下典史費長春加楚毒焉，七自經死，九誓雪兄枉，訴州不得直，訴監司，獄下州，仍不得直。

translations.literal: His family lived at Qingkou. His elder brother Qi had a land dispute with a neighbor and sued; Magistrate Wu Zhangyuan accepted the neighbor's bribe, arrested Qi, and had the clerk Fei Changchun apply cruel torture until Qi hanged himself. Jiu swore to clear his brother's wrong, appealed to the prefecture without justice, then to the surveillance commissioner; the case was sent down to the prefecture and still was not righted.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived at Qingkou. Elder brother Qi sued a neighbor over land. Magistrate Wu Zhangyuan took the neighbor's bribe, had Qi arrested, and ordered clerk Fei Changchun to torture him until Qi hanged himself. Jiu vowed to vindicate his brother, appealed to the prefecture and then the surveillance circuit, but each time the case was sent back without justice.

sentences.zh: 走京師，訴都察院，命下江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: He went to the capital and appealed to the Censorate; the court ordered the case sent to the Jiangsu governor.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Beijing and petitioned the Censorate, which referred the case to the Jiangsu governor.

sentences.zh: 元、長春賂承審官，責九健訟，加非刑，而令九所親關說，啗以重利，九不應。

translations.literal: Zhangyuan and Changchun bribed the reviewing officials, charged Jiu with vexatious litigation, and inflicted illegal punishments; they also had Jiu's kin intercede and tempted him with great gain, but he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangyuan and Changchun bribed the judges, accused Jiu of malicious litigation, and tortured him further. They sent relatives to offer him rich bribes; he refused.

sentences.zh: 九憤且楚，發病，​​元等賄醫將毒九。

translations.literal: Jiu, angry and in pain, fell ill; Zhangyuan and the others bribed a physician to poison him.
translations.idiomatic: Writhing in anger and pain, Jiu fell ill. Zhangyuan and his allies bribed a doctor to poison him.

sentences.zh: 會按察使陳繼昌至，親鞫，九得直。

translations.literal: When Surveillance Commissioner Chen Jichang arrived, he heard the case in person and Jiu obtained justice.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Chen Jichang arrived, heard the case himself, and Jiu at last won justice.

sentences.zh: 獄成，黜元，戍長春，誅縣役二。

translations.literal: When the case concluded, Zhangyuan was dismissed, Changchun was banished to military service, and two county runners were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The case closed: Zhangyuan was removed from office, Changchun was exiled to frontier service, and two county runners were put to death.

sentences.zh: 九歎曰：「兄枉雪，死無憾！」

translations.literal: Jiu sighed and said: "My brother's wrong is cleared—I can die without regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiu sighed, "My brother is vindicated. I can die content."

sentences.zh: 歸未至，卒。

translations.literal: Before he reached home on the return journey, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the road home.

sentences.zh: 青口士民具鼓樂迎其喪。

translations.literal: The gentry and common people of Qingkou went out with drums and music to welcome his coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qingkou met his coffin with drums and music.

sentences.zh: 張某，甘肅通渭人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mou was a native of Tongwei in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mou was from Tongwei in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆貧，為木工，相友愛。

translations.literal: The brothers were all poor and worked as carpenters, loving one another.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers were poor carpenters who loved each other dearly.

sentences.zh: 將析產，兄曰：「均之。」

translations.literal: When they were about to divide the property, the elder brother said: "Let us share equally."
translations.idiomatic: About to divide the estate, the elder brother said, "Let us split it evenly."

sentences.zh: 弟曰：「弟子一，而兄之子五，如兄言，弟子則富矣！

translations.literal: The younger brother said: "I have one son and you have five. If we follow your plan, my branch will be rich!
translations.idiomatic: The younger said, "I have one son; you have five. Your way makes my line wealthy.

sentences.zh: 諸侄獨非父母孫乎？

translations.literal: Are the nephews not also our parents' grandchildren?
translations.idiomatic: Are your nephews not our parents' grandchildren as well?

sentences.zh: 當視人為分。」

translations.literal: We should divide by number of persons."
translations.idiomatic: We should divide by head count."

sentences.zh: 兄曰：「不可，父母先有子，未嘗有孫。」

translations.literal: The elder brother said: "That will not do—when our parents were alive they had sons, not yet grandsons."
translations.idiomatic: The elder refused: "When our parents lived they had sons, not grandsons."

sentences.zh: 議不決，乃析為三，兄二而弟一。

translations.literal: Unable to agree, they divided into three shares—two for the elder and one for the younger.
translations.idiomatic: They could not settle it and split the estate in three: two parts to the elder, one to the younger.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆逾八十，常言：「誰先死，必呼與俱去。」

translations.literal: Both brothers passed eighty and often said: "Whoever dies first must call the other to go together."
translations.idiomatic: Past eighty, they often said, "Whoever dies first must call the other along."

sentences.zh: 兄卒，弟慟幾絕，不食七日，亦卒。

translations.literal: When the elder died, the younger grieved almost to death, fasted seven days, and died as well.
translations.idiomatic: The elder died; the younger grieved until he nearly perished, refused food for seven days, and followed him.

sentences.zh: 程含光，安徽休寧人。

translations.literal: Cheng Hanguang was a native of Xiuning in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hanguang was from Xiuning in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 出遊，得貲以養親。

translations.literal: He traveled abroad and used his earnings to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled for work and used his earnings to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 嘗偕弟自六安歸，策蹇經篛嶺。

translations.literal: Once he was returning from Lu'an with his younger brother, riding a donkey over Zhuo Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Once he and his brother were returning from Lu'an on donkeys, crossing Zhuo Ridge.

sentences.zh: 日暮風起，虎突出，攫弟去。

translations.literal: At dusk the wind rose; a tiger burst out and seized his brother away.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a wind sprang up and a tiger leaped out and carried off his brother.

sentences.zh: 含光驚墜地，持短鞭力追，左手據虎頸，右以鞭捶虎，大呼震山谷。

translations.literal: Hanguang fell in shock, seized a short whip and pursued with all his strength, gripped the tiger's neck with his left hand and beat it with the whip in his right, shouting until the valleys rang.
translations.idiomatic: Hanguang fell from his mount, snatched a riding crop, and chased the beast. He seized its neck with his left hand and lashed it with his right, roaring until the hills echoed.

sentences.zh: 虎舍弟嵎吼，含光負弟疾趨投嶺下旅舍。

translations.literal: The tiger released his brother on a slope and roared; Hanguang carried his brother in haste to an inn below the ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger dropped his brother on a hillside and roared off. Hanguang hoisted his brother on his back and ran to an inn below the pass.

sentences.zh: 弟息僅屬，灌以湯，徐甦，肩創十餘，血淋漓。

translations.literal: His brother's breath barely remained; they gave him broth and he slowly revived, with more than ten wounds on his shoulder, blood streaming.
translations.idiomatic: His brother was barely breathing. They warmed broth and brought him round. More than ten gashes on his shoulder ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 人言虎牙毒，血不盡且死，含光吮之，血盡出，乃瘥。

translations.literal: People said tiger fangs are poisonous and he would die unless the blood was fully drawn; Hanguang sucked the wounds until the blood was out, and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: They said tiger venom would kill him unless the blood was drawn. Hanguang sucked the wounds clean, and his brother healed.

sentences.zh: 其後含光卒，弟每言遇虎事，解衣示人，輒流涕不巳。

translations.literal: Later Hanguang died; whenever his brother spoke of the tiger encounter he would bare his shoulders to show others and weep without end.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanguang died, his brother would tell the story, bare his scarred shoulders, and weep without end.

sentences.zh: 陳福，福建永春人。

translations.literal: Chen Fu was a native of Yongchun in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fu was from Yongchun in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 居西溪，同居十二世，家範簡肅。

translations.literal: He lived at Xixi; twelve generations dwelt together under a household code that was plain and strict.
translations.idiomatic: At Xixi his clan lived together for twelve generations under a plain, austere household rule.

sentences.zh: 世以一人督家事，子孫率教醇樸，未有訟者。

translations.literal: Each generation one person supervised household affairs; descendants were uniformly taught to be honest and simple, and there were no lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: One head managed the household each generation. The clan was taught simplicity and honesty, and no one ever went to court.

sentences.zh: 譙衿，湖南沅江人。

translations.literal: Qiao Jin was a native of Yuanjiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Jin was from Yuanjiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 同居七世，有家訓二十條，喪祭無失禮。

translations.literal: Seven generations lived together; there were twenty household precepts, and funerals and sacrifices never fell short of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations lived as one household under twenty family precepts; funerals and sacrifices never missed proper rite.

sentences.zh: 黃成富，福建連江人。

translations.literal: Huang Chengfu was a native of Lianjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chengfu was from Lianjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 同居六世，子弟各執其業。

translations.literal: Six generations lived together; sons and younger kin each pursued his trade.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations lived together, each member keeping to his trade.

sentences.zh: 方田作，諸婦饁，以一婦守家，視臥兒於筐，飢則哺，不問何人子。

translations.literal: When the fields were worked, the women brought food; one woman stayed home and watched sleeping infants in baskets—if hungry she nursed them, without asking whose child.
translations.idiomatic: At planting time the women brought meals to the fields. One stayed home with infants in baskets; if a child cried for food she nursed it, never asking whose it was.

sentences.zh: 懸衣於桁，共衣之，垢則澣，不問何人衣。

translations.literal: Clothes hung on rafters and were worn in common; when soiled they were washed, without asking whose garment.
translations.idiomatic: Clothes hung on beams for all to wear; when dirty they were washed, with no inquiry as to owner.

sentences.zh: 雍睦無間言。

translations.literal: Harmony was complete and there was no discord.
translations.idiomatic: The clan lived in harmony without a word of strife.

sentences.zh: 李長茂，福建海澄人。

translations.literal: Li Changmao was a native of Haicheng in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changmao was from Haicheng in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 同居四世，建祠，置祭田，立義學，著家規、法戒各十條示子孫。

translations.literal: Four generations lived together; he built an ancestral hall, set aside sacrificial fields, founded a charity school, and wrote ten articles each of household regulations and admonitions for descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations lived as one. He built a clan hall, endowed sacrificial land, founded a charity school, and wrote ten household rules and ten admonitions for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 子五福，順治六年進士，官刑部侍郎，兄弟八人皆友愛。

translations.literal: His son Wufu passed the civil examination in the sixth year of Shunzhi and served as vice minister of justice; all eight brothers were affectionate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wufu became a jinshi in Shunzhi 6 and rose to vice minister of justice; all eight brothers remained devoted to one another.

sentences.zh: 任天篤，河南偃師人。

translations.literal: Ren Tiandu was a native of Yanshi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Tiandu was from Yanshi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，巡撫何裕成言天篤九世同居，高宗賜以詩，賚鏹帛，表宅里。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign, Governor He Yucheng reported that Tiandu had nine generations living together; the Gaozong Emperor bestowed a poem, gave silks and cash, and honored his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong era, Governor He Yucheng reported nine generations under one roof in Tiandu's clan. The Qianlong Emperor granted a poem, silks, and cash, and honored his household.

sentences.zh: 初，天篤祖開昌生五子，欲定議不析產，觀諸子意。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tiandu's ancestor Kaichang had five sons and wished to settle on not dividing the estate, observing the sons' intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Tiandu's ancestor Kaichang had five sons and wanted the family to keep the estate undivided, so he watched how they would act.

sentences.zh: 納金麥囷中，子士堯、士舜得以告，開昌曰：「此天賜，汝二人取之！」

translations.literal: He placed gold in the wheat granary; sons Shiyao and Shishun were able to report it. Kaichang said: "This is Heaven's gift—take it, you two!"
translations.idiomatic: He hid gold in the wheat bin. Sons Shiyao and Shishun found it and told him. Kaichang said, "Heaven sent this—take it, both of you!"

sentences.zh: 以「子無私蓄」對。

translations.literal: They answered: "Sons should have no private hoard."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "A son should keep no private stash."

sentences.zh: 開昌悅，乃定議不析產。

translations.literal: Kaichang was pleased and then fixed the decision not to divide the property.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Kaichang made the clan vow never to split the estate.

sentences.zh: 宗經、傳，為家訓，教子弟毋侈，毋急利，毋入城市，毋傳述時事，務耕田讀書，惟許學醫，亦毋取酬，不則執百工業以佐家。

translations.literal: The classics were taken as household precepts: teach the young not to be extravagant, not to chase quick profit, not to enter cities, not to spread news of the times; devote yourselves to farming and study; only medicine was permitted, and without fee—otherwise practice a craft to support the household.
translations.idiomatic: The classics became family law: no luxury, no greed, no trips to town, no gossip about current affairs—only farm and study. Medicine alone was allowed, and never for pay; otherwise take up a trade to help the house.

sentences.zh: 婦初至，長者以家訓教之，不率，令暫還母家，悟，乃迎歸。

translations.literal: When a bride first arrived, elders taught her the household code; if she did not follow it, she was sent temporarily to her mother's home, and when she understood, she was welcomed back.
translations.idiomatic: New brides were taught the family rules. Those who would not obey were sent home until they understood, then brought back.

sentences.zh: 平居布衣椎髻操作，毋私饋，毋飾容觀，毋適私室。

translations.literal: In daily life they wore plain cloth and wore their hair in a simple knot while working; no private gifts, no adornment, no visiting private chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Daily life meant plain dress, simple hair, and labor—no private gifts, no cosmetics, no sneaking off to private rooms.

sentences.zh: 年五十不執役，寡毋入廚，稍厚其衣食。

translations.literal: At fifty one was excused from labor; widows did not enter the kitchen, and their food and clothing were somewhat better provided.
translations.idiomatic: At fifty one stopped heavy work. Widows did not cook; their food and clothing were a little better than others'.

sentences.zh: 女適人寡，毋再嫁。

translations.literal: If a daughter married and was widowed, she must not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: A widowed daughter-in-law must not marry again.

sentences.zh: 至天篤，上溯開昌祖光玉，下見玄孫瑞豐，通九世男婦百六十餘人共爨。

translations.literal: By Tiandu's time, tracing up to Kaichang's ancestor Guangyu and down to great-great-grandson Ruifeng, nine generations of men and women—more than one hundred sixty persons—shared one kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: By Tiandu's day the line ran from ancestor Guangyu through Kaichang to great-great-grandson Ruifeng—nine generations, more than one hundred sixty men and women eating from one pot.

sentences.zh: 吏問天篤何術能不析產，天篤曰：「不忍也！」

translations.literal: An official asked Tiandu by what art the estate was not divided; Tiandu said: "By forbearance!"
translations.idiomatic: An official asked how they kept the estate whole. Tiandu said, "We could not bear to split it."

sentences.zh: 人傳其語，謂視張公藝書「忍」字義尤大而遠。

translations.literal: People spread his words and said the meaning surpassed even Zhang Gongyi's character for "forbearance."
translations.idiomatic: People repeated his words and said he had gone even deeper than Zhang Gongyi's famous "forbearance."

sentences.zh: 其後傅麟瑞、張璘，皆以七世同居賜詩旌獎。

translations.literal: Later Fu Linrui and Zhang Lin were both rewarded with imperial poems for seven generations living together.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fu Linrui and Zhang Lin likewise received imperial poems for seven generations under one roof.

sentences.zh: 麟瑞，魯山諸生；

translations.literal: Linrui was a licentiate of Lushan;
translations.idiomatic: Linrui was a licentiate of Lushan.

sentences.zh: 璘，涇陽諸生。

translations.literal: Lin was a licentiate of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin was a licentiate of Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 趙一桂，不知其邑裡。

translations.literal: Zhao Yigui's native place is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yigui's home district is unknown.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，以省祭官署昌平州吏目，被檄為莊烈帝、後營葬。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chongzhen reign he served as acting clerk of Changping prefecture on provincial sacrifice duty and was ordered to arrange burial for the Chongzhen Emperor and empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Chongzhen he was acting clerk at Changping on sacrifice duty and was ordered to bury the Chongzhen Emperor and his empress.

sentences.zh: 師入關，定京師，列狀申州，略曰：「三月二十五日奉順天府檄，穿田妃壙，葬崇禎帝、後。

translations.literal: When the army entered the pass and the capital was secured, he submitted a memorial to the prefecture, in summary: "On the twenty-fifth day of the third month I received orders from Shuntian prefecture to open the consort Tian's tomb and bury the Chongzhen Emperor and empress.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qing secured Beijing he petitioned the prefecture: "On the twenty-fifth of the third month I received Shuntian's order to open Consort Tian's tomb and bury the Chongzhen Emperor and empress.

sentences.zh: 四月初三日發引，初四日下窆。

translations.literal: The procession set out on the third day of the fourth month and interment was on the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral left on the third of the fourth month; burial was on the fourth.

sentences.zh: 州庫如洗，葬日促，監葬官禮部主事許作梅無策，職與義士孫繁祉等十人，斂錢三百四十千，僦夫穿壙。

translations.literal: The prefectural treasury was empty and the burial day pressed; Supervising Burial Officer Xu Zuomei of the Ministry of Rites had no plan. I and ten righteous men including Sun Fanzhi raised three hundred forty thousand cash and hired laborers to open the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury was bare and time was short. Burial officer Xu Zuomei of the Ministry of Rites was at a loss. I and ten volunteers led by Sun Fanzhi raised 340,000 cash and hired diggers.

sentences.zh: 至初四日，羨道開通，啟壙宮門入，享殿三間，陳祭品。

translations.literal: By the fourth the spirit way was opened; the tomb gate was entered and there was a offering hall of three bays with sacrificial goods set out.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth the passage was open. We entered the tomb gate to a three-bay offering hall laid with sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 中設石案一，懸鐙二。

translations.literal: In the center stood one stone table with two lamps hanging.
translations.idiomatic: A stone table stood in the center with two lamps hung above it.

sentences.zh: 旁列錦綺繒幣五色，俱生存所用器物奁具，皆貯以硃紅木笥。

translations.literal: Beside it were brocades and silks of five colors—all objects and chests used in life, stored in cinnabar-red wooden boxes.
translations.idiomatic: Brocades and silks in five colors lay beside it—life goods and trousseau chests in red-lacquered boxes.

sentences.zh: 左傍石床一，床上氍毹衾枕。

translations.literal: To the left was a stone couch with rugs, quilts, and pillows upon it.
translations.idiomatic: To the left a stone couch bore rugs, quilts, and pillows.

sentences.zh: 又啟中羨門，內大殿九間，中為石床，置田妃棺槨。

translations.literal: The inner spirit gate was opened; within was a great hall of nine bays with a stone couch in the center bearing Consort Tian's coffin.
translations.idiomatic: We opened the inner gate to a nine-bay hall and a central stone couch holding Consort Tian's coffin.

sentences.zh: 帝、後梓宮至，停席棚，陳羊豕、金銀紙錁、祭品。

translations.literal: When the emperor's and empress's coffins arrived, they rested under a mat shed; sheep, pigs, gold and silver paper ingots, and offerings were set out.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial coffins arrived we sheltered them under mats and set out sheep, pigs, paper ingots, and offerings.

sentences.zh: 率眾伏謁，哭，盡哀。

translations.literal: Leading the crowd he bowed prostrate, wept, and mourned to the full.
translations.idiomatic: He led all present in prostration and weeping until grief was spent.

sentences.zh: 職躬督夫役移田妃柩於右，奉週皇后梓宮於左，乃安先帝梓宮居中。

translations.literal: He personally supervised the laborers in moving Consort Tian's bier to the right, placing Empress Zhou's coffin on the left, and setting the late emperor's coffin in the center.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw moving Consort Tian's bier to the right, Empress Zhou's to the left, and the late emperor's to the center.

sentences.zh: 先帝有棺無槨，移田妃槨用之。

translations.literal: The late emperor had a coffin but no outer shell; Consort Tian's shell was moved to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had an inner coffin but no outer shell; Consort Tian's shell was used for his.

sentences.zh: 梓宮前各設香案祭器，職手燃萬年鐙，度不滅。

translations.literal: Before each coffin incense tables and ritual vessels were set; he lit the eternal lamps by hand, intending they should not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Incense tables were placed before each coffin. He lit the eternal lamps himself, meaning them never to die.

sentences.zh: 久之，事畢，掩中羨，閉外羨門，复土與地平。

translations.literal: After a long while the work was done; the inner spirit path was closed, the outer spirit gate shut, and earth heaped level with the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When all was done they sealed the inner passage, closed the outer gate, and heaped earth level with the ground.

sentences.zh: 初六日，又率諸人祭​​奠號哭，呼集居民百餘人，畚土起塚，又築塚牆高五尺有奇。

translations.literal: On the sixth he again led the men in offering and wailing, called together more than a hundred residents to mound earth and build a tomb wall more than five feet high.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth he led mourning again, gathered a hundred villagers to raise the mound, and built a tomb wall over five feet high.

sentences.zh: 幸本朝定鼎，為先帝建陵殿三間，繚以周垣，使故主陵寢，不侵樵牧，雖三代開國，無以加之。

translations.literal: Fortunately our dynasty secured the realm and built a three-bay mausoleum hall ringed with a wall, so the former sovereign's resting place was not disturbed by woodcutters or herdsmen—even founding kings of the Three Dynasties did no more.
translations.idiomatic: The new dynasty built a three-bay hall and encircling wall so the late sovereign's tomb was safe from woodcutters and herds—even founders of the Three Dynasties did no more.

sentences.zh: 一時斂錢者：繁祉，諸生劉汝樸、白紳、徐魁、李某、鄧科、趙永健、劉應元、楊道、王政行，皆州民。」

translations.literal: Those who raised funds at the time were: Fanzhi; licentiates Liu Rupu, Bai Shen, Xu Kui, Li Mou, Deng Ke, Zhao Yongjian, Liu Yingyuan; Yang Dao and Wang Zhengxing—all men of the prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Those who gave money were Fanzhi; licentiates Liu Rupu, Bai Shen, Xu Kui, Li Mou, Deng Ke, Zhao Yongjian, Liu Yingyuan; Yang Dao and Wang Zhengxing—all local men."

sentences.zh: 康熙中，嘉興譚吉璁至昌平，得故吏牘，採入所為肅松錄，邵長蘅又為之文，謂是時李自成據京師，禮部主事改禮政府屬，蓋一桂不知自成所改官制，而政行有子乞韓菼表墓，亦書其事。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign Tan Jijun of Jiaxing came to Changping, obtained old clerk documents, and included them in his Susong lu; Shao Changheng also wrote of it, saying that then Li Zicheng held Beijing and a Ministry of Rites director was made a subordinate of the Ministry of Rites under the rebel regime—Yigui did not know the regime Li Zicheng had imposed, while Zhengxing's son asked Han Tan for a tomb inscription, which also recorded the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi, Tan Jijun of Jiaxing found old clerk papers at Changping and put them in his Susong lu. Shao Changheng wrote that Li Zicheng then held Beijing and turned a Ministry director into a rebel post—Yigui did not know that regime. Zhengxing's son later had Han Tan compose a tomb inscription recording the same events.

sentences.zh: 黃調鼎，字鹽梅，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Huang Diaoding, style name Yanmei, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Diaoding, style Yanmei, was from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 其女兄，明福王由崧妃也。

translations.literal: His elder sister was consort to the Ming Prince Fu, Zhu Yousong.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister had been consort to the Ming Prince of Fu, Zhu Yousong.

sentences.zh: 早卒，葬洛陽。

translations.literal: She died early and was buried at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: She died young and was buried at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 福王稱帝南京，追爵妃父奇瑞洛中伯，以其長子九鼎襲，亦官調鼎。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu declared himself emperor at Nanjing, he posthumously ennobled the consort's father Qirui as Marquis of Luozhong; his eldest son Jiuding inherited, and Diaoding also received office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yousong took the throne at Nanjing he made the consort's father Qirui Marquis of Luozhong posthumously. Eldest son Jiuding inherited; Diaoding also received office.

sentences.zh: 福王選立後、妃，巡撫山陰祁彪佳之女與焉，命以彪佳少女妻調鼎。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu chose an heir and consorts, the daughter of Shanyin magistrate Qi Biaojia was among them; he ordered Biaojia's younger daughter given in marriage to Diaoding.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince chose an heir and consorts, Qi Biaojia's daughter of Shanyin was among the candidates. The court married Biaojia's younger daughter to Diaoding.

sentences.zh: 南都破，九鼎降，馬士英挾福王母鄒太后至浙江。

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital fell, Jiuding surrendered; Ma Shiying took the Prince of Fu's mother Empress Dowager Zou to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell, Jiuding surrendered. Ma Shiying escorted Empress Dowager Zou to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，太后匿山陰民家，調鼎走依祁氏，與相聞。

translations.literal: After defeat the empress dowager hid in a Shanyin household; Diaoding fled to the Qi family and kept in contact.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat the empress dowager hid with a Shanyin family. Diaoding took refuge with the Qis and stayed in touch.

sentences.zh: 福王死京師，求得其柩，載歸洛陽，葬故妃園。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu died in the capital, they sought his coffin, carried it back to Luoyang, and buried it in the former consort's garden.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince died in Beijing they recovered his coffin, brought it to Luoyang, and buried it in the consort's old garden.

sentences.zh: 迎鄒太后奉養，至卒，葬福恭王園。

translations.literal: They welcomed Empress Dowager Zou to support her until her death, when she was buried in the garden of Prince Fu Gong.
translations.idiomatic: They brought Empress Dowager Zou home and cared for her until she died, then buried her in Prince Fu Gong's garden.

sentences.zh: 調鼎棄諸生，不出。

translations.literal: Diaoding abandoned his licentiate status and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Diaoding gave up his licentiate standing and lived in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 楊藝，字碩父，廣西臨桂人，大學士瞿式耜客也。

translations.literal: Yang Yi, style name Shuofu, was a native of Lingui in Guangxi and a client of Grand Secretary Qu Shisi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi, style Shuofu, was from Lingui in Guangxi and a retainer of Grand Secretary Qu Shisi.

sentences.zh: 闊略無所忌諱，同幕者稱為痴藝，因以自號。

translations.literal: Broad and heedless of taboo, colleagues in the secretariat called him "Mad Yi," and he took it as his sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: Carefree and blunt, colleagues called him "Mad Yi," and he adopted the name.

sentences.zh: 已，終不合去。

translations.literal: In time he left, unable to get along.
translations.idiomatic: In time he left, unable to work with them.

sentences.zh: 孔有德徇廣西，破桂林，執式耜及總督張同敞，不​​屈死，藝衰絰懸紙錢滿衣，號哭營、市間，請斂式耜，有德聞而義焉，遂許之，令並斂同敞。

translations.literal: Kong Youde swept Guangxi, took Guilin, and seized Qu Shisi and Governor Zhang Tongchang, who died unyielding. Yi wore mourning hemp and hung paper money over his clothes, wailing through camps and markets to ask burial for Shisi. Youde heard and honored it, permitted it, and ordered Tongchang buried as well.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Youde overran Guangxi, took Guilin, and executed Qu Shisi and Governor Zhang Tongchang, who would not submit. Yi dressed in mourning hemp hung with paper money and wailed through camps and markets to beg Shisi's burial. Youde was moved, agreed, and ordered Tongchang buried too.

sentences.zh: 有姚端者，式耜門人。

translations.literal: There was Yao Duan, a disciple of Shisi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Duan was Shisi's student.

sentences.zh: 藝與謀，斂式耜及同敞，淺葬風洞山麓，築室於旁，守墓不去。

translations.literal: Yi plotted with him to bury Shisi and Tongchang, giving them shallow graves at the foot of Fengdong Mountain, built a hut beside them, and guarded the tombs without leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Yao buried Shisi and Tongchang shallowly at Fengdong Mountain, built a hut, and refused to leave the graves.

sentences.zh: 時明給事中金堡去為僧，將上書有德乞斂式耜等，知藝先之，乃罷。

translations.literal: Then Ming Supervising Secretary Jin Bao had become a monk and was about to petition Youde to bury Shisi and the others; learning Yi had acted first, he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Ming secretary Jin Bao had become a monk and meant to petition Youde for the burials; learning Yi had acted first, he gave up.

sentences.zh: 以書稿寄式耜子，頗流傳人間，而罕知藝者。

translations.literal: He sent manuscripts to Shisi's son; they circulated among people, yet few knew of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent manuscripts to Shisi's son. They spread, yet few knew of Yi.

sentences.zh: 堡紀其事甚詳，且曰：「以吾書掩藝，吾為竊名，瞿氏子為負德。」

translations.literal: Bao recorded the affair in detail and said: "To use my writing to overshadow Yi is for me to steal fame; Shisi's son would be ungrateful."
translations.idiomatic: Bao wrote at length and said, "To let my account overshadow Yi is to steal his credit; Shisi's son would be ungrateful."

sentences.zh: 咸默，字大咸，江南山陽人。

translations.literal: Xian Mo, style name Dacheng, was a native of Shanyang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xian Mo, style Dacheng, was from Shanyang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 明諸生，侍郎左懋第客也。

translations.literal: A Ming licentiate, he was a client of Vice Minister Zuo Maodi.
translations.idiomatic: A Ming licentiate, he was retainer to Vice Minister Zuo Maodi.

sentences.zh: 福王遣懋第等詣京師，默與司務陳用極，副將艾大選，游擊王一斌，都司張良佐、王廷佐，守備劉統從。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu sent Maodi and others to the capital, Mo went with Chief of Staff Chen Yongji, Vice General Ai Daxuan, Mobile Corps Commander Wang Yibin, and garrison officers Zhang Liangzuo, Wang Tingzuo, and Liu Tong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu sent Maodi to Beijing, Mo went with Chen Yongji, Ai Daxuan, Wang Yibin, and officers Zhang Liangzuo, Wang Tingzuo, and Liu Tong.

sentences.zh: 使事畢，留勿遣。

translations.literal: When the mission ended they were detained and not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission ended they were held and not released.

sentences.zh: 大選從令薙發，懋第怒笞之，自殺。

translations.literal: Daxuan obeyed the order to shave his head; Maodi angrily flogged him and he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Daxuan obeyed the order to shave his head. Maodi flogged him in rage; he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 南京破，懋第與用極、一斌、良佐、廷佐、統，皆以不屈死。

translations.literal: When Nanjing fell, Maodi, Yongji, Yibin, Liangzuo, Tingzuo, and Tong all died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell, Maodi, Yongji, Yibin, Liangzuo, Tingzuo, and Tong all died refusing submission.

sentences.zh: 默送懋第喪歸葬萊陽，又送用極喪歸葬崑山，一斌等為淺葬京師郊外。

translations.literal: Mo escorted Maodi's coffin home for burial at Laiyang, then escorted Yongji's for burial at Kunshan; Yibin and the others received shallow burial outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mo brought Maodi's body home to Laiyang and Yongji's to Kunshan. Yibin and the rest were buried shallowly outside Beijing.

sentences.zh: 默託堪輿術遊四方，嘗作哭萊陽詩以吊懋第，淒楚，人不忍讀。

translations.literal: Mo traveled the realm claiming geomancy; he once wrote a poem mourning Laiyang to lament Maodi—so plaintive that people could not bear to read it.
translations.idiomatic: Mo wandered as a geomancer and wrote a lament for Laiyang so piercing readers could hardly bear it.

sentences.zh: 李晉福，直隸景州人。

translations.literal: Li Jinfu was a native of Jingzhou in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinfu was from Jingzhou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 事諸生趙遵譜為僮。

translations.literal: He served the licentiate Zhao Zunpu as a bondservant.
translations.idiomatic: He was bondservant to licentiate Zhao Zunpu.

sentences.zh: 師入塞，略地至州，遵譜方出遊，騎​​而行，晉福從，倉卒被掠去，家人不知也。

translations.literal: When the army entered the frontier and overran the prefecture, Zunpu was traveling and riding; Jinfu followed and was suddenly seized—his family did not know.
translations.idiomatic: When the Manchu army raided the district, Zunpu was out riding and Jinfu with him. They were seized; the family knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 越數日，晉福潛還，告家人，即復從遵譜出塞。

translations.literal: After several days Jinfu slipped back, told the family, and then went out again to follow Zunpu beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Jinfu stole home, told the family, and went back beyond the pass to Zunpu.

sentences.zh: 遵譜馬為人奪，與晉福徒跣行。

translations.literal: Zunpu's horse was taken by others; he and Jinfu walked barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: Zunpu's horse was taken. Master and servant walked barefoot.

sentences.zh: 久之，有騎過，則遵譜馬也。

translations.literal: After a long while a rider passed—it was Zunpu's horse.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward a rider passed—it was Zunpu's horse.

sentences.zh: 遵譜直前欲奪之，騎者抽刀斫遵譜僕，幾死。

translations.literal: Zunpu went straight forward to seize it; the rider drew a knife and hacked Zunpu's servant, nearly killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Zunpu rushed to reclaim it. The rider slashed his servant nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 晉福負歸為裡創，僅乃得愈。

translations.literal: Jinfu carried him back and dressed the wound; only with difficulty did he recover.
translations.idiomatic: Jinfu carried the man back and dressed his wounds until he barely recovered.

sentences.zh: 遵譜惷直，晉福力戒毋負氣取禍，在兵中稍久相習。

translations.literal: Zunpu was blunt and upright; Jinfu strongly warned him not to take offense and court disaster; in the army they gradually grew familiar.
translations.idiomatic: Zunpu was blunt and hot-tempered. Jinfu urged him not to provoke trouble. In the camp they slowly grew used to captivity.

sentences.zh: 晉福弟遵譜，有勞役，必代之。

translations.literal: When Jinfu's younger brother had corvée labor, he always took his place.
translations.idiomatic: When corvée fell on Jinfu's younger brother, he always took his place.

sentences.zh: 後三年，得間，遣遵譜亡歸。

translations.literal: Three years later he found an opening and sent Zunpu home to escape.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he found a chance and sent Zunpu home.

sentences.zh: 歸一年，晉福亦逃入塞。

translations.literal: A year after Zunpu returned, Jinfu also fled beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Jinfu escaped and followed him home.

sentences.zh: 胡端友，湖南寧鄉人，劉光初僕也。

translations.literal: Hu Duanyou was a native of Ningxiang in Hunan and servant to Liu Guangchu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Duanyou was from Ningxiang in Hunan, servant to Liu Guangchu.

sentences.zh: 順治初，光初妻胡遇寇，以幼子付端友，端友負而逃，寇逐之，力奔得脫。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi, Guangchu's wife Hu met bandits and entrusted her young son to Duanyou; Duanyou carried him and fled; the bandits pursued, but he ran with all his strength and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, Guangchu's wife Hu met bandits and gave her little son to Duanyou. He ran with the boy on his back and outpaced the pursuers.

sentences.zh: 至其家，釋負，僕，久之乃蘇。

translations.literal: Reaching the house he set down his burden; the servant collapsed and only after a long while revived.
translations.idiomatic: At home he set the child down and collapsed; long minutes passed before he woke.

sentences.zh: 胡死於寇，其子得成立。

translations.literal: Hu died at the hands of the bandits, but her son grew to adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: Mrs. Hu died in the raid, but the boy grew up.

sentences.zh: 至乾隆中，丁近二千，劉氏祀端友於祏。

translations.literal: By the Qianlong reign nearly two thousand ding had passed; the Liu clan enshrined Duanyou in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: By Qianlong, nearly two thousand ding later, the Lius placed Duanyou in the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 硃永慶，字長源，順天大興人，故明宣府巡撫之馮子也。

translations.literal: Zhu Yongqing, style name Changyuan, was a native of Daxing in Shuntian and son of the former Ming Xuanfu surveillance commissioner Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yongqing, style Changyuan, was from Daxing in Shuntian, son of the Ming Xuanfu surveillance commissioner Feng.

sentences.zh: 師入關，永慶見俘，隸漢軍正黃旗，僦屋居。

translations.literal: When the army entered the pass, Yongqing was taken captive, enrolled in the Plain Yellow Banner of the Han Army, and rented a house to live in.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing entered the pass Yongqing was captured, enrolled in the Han Plain Yellow Banner, and rented a room.

sentences.zh: 永慶修幹美髯，負氣節，好佛，主者賢之，將賜以婦，命視諸俘，恣所擇。

translations.literal: Yongqing was tall and handsome with a fine beard, proud of integrity, fond of Buddhism; his master esteemed him and was about to give him a wife, ordering him to look among the captives and choose as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: Tall, bearded, proud, and devout, he won his master's regard. The master meant to give him a wife and let him choose among the captives.

sentences.zh: 武進楊兆升，仕明官給事中，起兵死。

translations.literal: Yang Zhaosheng of Wujin had served the Ming as supervising secretary and died raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhaosheng of Wujin had been a Ming supervising secretary and died in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 妾姚見俘，薙發矢守節。

translations.literal: Concubine Yao was taken captive, shaved her head, and vowed to guard her chastity.
translations.idiomatic: His concubine Yao was captured, shaved her head, and swore to keep her chastity.

sentences.zh: 永慶夙聞之，乃自名故殉難宣府巡撫子，擇姚以請，引歸所居室。

translations.literal: Yongqing had long heard of her; he then named himself as son of the martyred Xuanfu commissioner and chose Yao, bringing her to his quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing had heard of her. He declared himself the martyred commissioner's son, chose Yao, and brought her to his room.

sentences.zh: 向夕，姚拜永慶乞哀，永慶曰：「吾將全夫人節，非特哀之而已。」

translations.literal: At evening Yao bowed to Yongqing begging mercy; Yongqing said: "I mean to preserve your integrity—not merely to pity you."
translations.idiomatic: That evening Yao begged him. He said, "I mean to preserve your honor—not merely to pity you."

sentences.zh: 乃誦佛至旦，凡三夕，居停覘知之，問曰：「君不近婦人，安用此贅疣？」

translations.literal: He then chanted Buddhist sutras until dawn—for three nights.
translations.idiomatic: He chanted sutras until dawn—for three nights.

sentences.zh: 永慶曰：「此縉紳婦，吾非欲妻之，欲完其節耳。

translations.literal: His landlord noticed and asked: "You do not approach women—what use is this encumbrance?"
translations.idiomatic: His landlord noticed and asked, "You won't touch her—why keep her here?

sentences.zh: 恐機洩，故且同室，然非誦佛不可。

translations.literal: Yongqing said: "This is a gentry wife; I do not wish to marry her but to complete her chastity.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "She is a gentlewoman's wife. I do not want her body—I want her honor intact.

sentences.zh: 乃為君偵得，幸終為吾諱。」

translations.literal: Fearing the plan would leak, we share a room for now, yet only chanting sutras will do. You discovered it by spying—please keep my secret to the end."
translations.idiomatic: Lest word leak out we share a room, but only prayer will do. You found out by watching—please keep my secret."

sentences.zh: 居停感焉，乃治別室以居姚。

translations.literal: The landlord was moved and prepared a separate room for Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the landlord gave Yao a room of her own.

sentences.zh: 久之，事聞於主者，主者益賢之，令姚寄書其家，以其母若弟來，予貲遣之還。

translations.literal: After a long while the matter reached his master, who esteemed him still more, had Yao write home, brought her mother and brother, and gave funds to send them back.
translations.idiomatic: In time his master heard, admired him more, had Yao write home, summoned her mother and brother, and sent them away with funds.

sentences.zh: 王某，江南如皋人，隸也。

translations.literal: Wang Mou was a bondservant of Rugao in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mou was a bondservant from Rugao in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治初，縣人許德溥坐不薙發死，妻當流，王欲脫之，思不得其策，夜不寐，其妻怪問之，語以故。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi, a townsman Xu Depu was put to death for refusing to shave his head; his wife was to be exiled. Wang wished to save her but could find no plan; he lay awake at night. His wife wondered and asked; he told her the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, Xu Depu of the town was executed for refusing to shave. His wife faced exile. Wang could find no plan and lay awake. His wife asked; he told her.

sentences.zh: 其妻曰：「此義舉也！

translations.literal: His wife said: "This is a righteous act!
translations.idiomatic: His wife said, "That is a righteous deed!

sentences.zh: 然非得一人代不可。」

translations.literal: Yet one must have someone to take her place."
translations.idiomatic: But someone must go in her stead."

sentences.zh: 王曰：

translations.literal: Wang said:
translations.idiomatic: Wang said,

sentences.zh: 「安所得代者？」

translations.literal: "Where could one find a substitute?"
translations.idiomatic: "Where could we find someone to take her place?"

sentences.zh: 其妻曰：「吾當成子義舉，原代行。」

translations.literal: His wife said: "I shall complete your righteous deed—I am willing to go in her stead."
translations.idiomatic: His wife said, "Let me finish what you began—I will go in her place."

sentences.zh: 王伏地叩頭謝。

translations.literal: Wang prostrated himself and kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Wang prostrated himself and kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 乃匿德溥妻，而以其妻行，行數千里，至流所。

translations.literal: He then hid Depu's wife and sent his own wife in her place; she traveled several thousand li to the place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: He hid Depu's wife and sent his own wife instead. She traveled thousands of li to the place of exile.

sentences.zh: 縣人義之，斂金贖歸，夫婦終老於家。

translations.literal: The townspeople honored their righteousness, collected funds to ransom her back, and the couple lived out their lives at home.
translations.idiomatic: Townspeople admired their righteousness, pooled money to buy her back, and the couple lived out their days at home.

sentences.zh: 張瑛，字玉採，山西汾陽人，居西官村。

translations.literal: Zhang Ying, style Yucai, was a native of Fenyang in Shanxi and lived in Xiguan Village.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying, style Yucai, was from Fenyang in Shanxi and lived in Xiguan Village.

sentences.zh: 順治六年，姜瓖亂，眾劫東官村趙氏，盡殺其人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shunzhi, Jiang Xiang rebelled; a mob raided the Zhao family of Dongguan Village and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shunzhi, Jiang Xiang rebelled. A mob raided the Zhao household of Dongguan Village and slaughtered everyone.

sentences.zh: 獨一子亡歸瑛，瑛納之，眾索焉，瑛不與。

translations.literal: Only one son escaped and fled to Ying; Ying took him in. The mob demanded him, but Ying would not surrender him.
translations.idiomatic: One son alone escaped to Ying, who sheltered him. The mob came for the boy; Ying refused to hand him over.

sentences.zh: 瓖亂定，瑛助趙氏子訟於官，誅劫者。

translations.literal: When Xiang's rebellion was suppressed, Ying helped the Zhao son bring suit in court and have the raiders executed.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang's rebellion was put down, Ying helped the Zhao son sue in court and have the raiders executed.

sentences.zh: 當亂急，村人將走避，瑛曰：「賊未至先走，能保必全乎？

translations.literal: When the turmoil was urgent and the villagers were about to flee, Ying said: "If you flee before the bandits arrive, can you be sure of escaping unscathed?
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis deepened and villagers prepared to flee, Ying said, "If you run before the bandits even arrive, can you be sure you'll come through whole?

sentences.zh: 孰若為守計！」

translations.literal: Would it not be better to plan for defense!"
translations.idiomatic: Better to make a stand!"

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「如無砦堡何！」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "But what if we have no fort!"
translations.idiomatic: The villagers said, "But we have no fort!"

sentences.zh: 瑛曰：「砦堡誠不可猝為，環村而溝焉，其可。」

translations.literal: Ying said: "A fort truly cannot be built in haste, but digging a trench around the village—that can be done."
translations.idiomatic: Ying said, "A fort can't be thrown up overnight—but a trench ringed around the village can."

sentences.zh: 遂為溝，務深廣。

translations.literal: So they dug a trench, making it as deep and wide as possible.
translations.idiomatic: They dug a trench and made it as deep and wide as they could.

sentences.zh: 瑛家有樓，貯村人財物其中。

translations.literal: Ying's family had a tower in which the villagers' goods were stored.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's family owned a tower where villagers stored their valuables.

sentences.zh: 既而賊大至，逾溝，村人退保樓。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits came in force, crossed the trench, and the villagers retreated to defend the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the bandits arrived in strength, crossed the trench, and the villagers fell back to the tower.

sentences.zh: 瑛見賊渠據胡床坐而指揮，發石中之，立斃。

translations.literal: Ying saw the bandit leader seated on a folding chair directing operations; he loosed a stone that struck him and killed him instantly.
translations.idiomatic: Ying saw the bandit chief seated on a camp chair giving orders. He hurled a stone that struck true and killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 餘賊怒攻樓，取薪將焚，眾汲井以救。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits angrily attacked the tower, gathered firewood to burn it, and the people drew water from the well to fight the fire.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the bandits stormed the tower and piled firewood to burn it. The villagers drew water from the well to fight the flames.

sentences.zh: 持數日，乃稍稍去。

translations.literal: After several days the bandits gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They held out for days until the bandits slowly dispersed.

sentences.zh: 瑛率眾出擊之，賊奔潰，村以得全。

translations.literal: Ying led the crowd out to attack them; the bandits fled in rout and the village was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Ying led a counterattack; the bandits broke and fled, and the village was saved.

sentences.zh: 瑛家饒，歲終，必出粟週鄰里。

translations.literal: Ying's family was wealthy; at the end of each year he always distributed grain to his neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: The Ying household was prosperous. Every year at year's end he gave grain to the neighbors.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十六年，飢，縣民鬻田，貶其值，瑛輒收之，得田且千畝。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Kangxi there was famine; county people sold their fields at depressed prices, and Ying bought them up, acquiring nearly a thousand mu of land.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of Kangxi famine struck. County people sold their fields at cut rates, and Ying bought them up until he held nearly a thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 明年大穰，瑛榜諸村曰：「原贖者聽。」

translations.literal: The next year brought a great harvest; Ying posted notices in the villages saying: "Those who wish to redeem may do so."
translations.idiomatic: The next year brought a bumper harvest. Ying posted notices in the villages: "All who wish to redeem their land may do so."

sentences.zh: 不十日盡贖去。

translations.literal: Within ten days all the land was redeemed.
translations.idiomatic: In less than ten days every plot was redeemed.

sentences.zh: 瑛卒，年九十有一。

translations.literal: Ying died at the age of ninety-one.
translations.idiomatic: Ying died at ninety-one.

sentences.zh: 郭氏僕，失姓名，山西聞喜郭景汾家僕也。

translations.literal: A servant of the Guo family, name lost, was a servant in the household of Guo Jingfen of Wenxi in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: A servant of the Guo family, name unknown, served in the household of Guo Jingfen of Wenxi in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 姜瓖反，縣人章惇為亂，殺景汾祖及父。

translations.literal: When Jiang Xiang rebelled, a townsman Zhang Dun raised a disturbance and killed Jingfen's grandfather and father.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Xiang rebelled, a local man named Zhang Dun joined the turmoil and killed Jingfen's grandfather and father.

sentences.zh: 景汾方三歲，僕負之走，得免。

translations.literal: Jingfen was only three; the servant carried him on his back and fled, and the boy escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfen was only three. The servant carried him on his back and fled through the chaos, and the boy survived.

sentences.zh: 瓖敗，惇降，得官。

translations.literal: When Xiang was defeated, Dun surrendered and obtained an official post.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang's defeat Dun surrendered and was given an official post.

sentences.zh: 景汾讀書成進士，上僕義，被旌。

translations.literal: Jingfen studied and became a jinshi; he reported the servant's righteousness, and the servant was commended.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfen passed the examinations and became a jinshi. He reported the servant's loyalty, and the court commended him.

sentences.zh: 景汾圖復仇，顧惇已遇赦，知縣邵伯麟為之解，令惇謁景汾祖、父墓，且詣景汾謝。

translations.literal: Jingfen plotted revenge, but Dun had already been pardoned; Magistrate Shao Bolin mediated, ordering Dun to visit the graves of Jingfen's grandfather and father and also go to Jingfen to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfen planned revenge, but Dun had already been amnestied. Magistrate Shao Bolin intervened, ordering Dun to pay respects at the graves of Jingfen's grandfather and father and then come to Jingfen to apologize.

sentences.zh: 居無何，景汾擊殺

translations.literal: Before long, Jingfen struck and killed
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward Jingfen attacked and killed

sentences.zh: 惇，斷其首祭祖、父，而身詣獄。

translations.literal: Dun, cut off his head to sacrifice before his grandfather and father, and then went himself to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Dun, severed his head as an offering before his grandfather and father, and then surrendered himself to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 伯麟義景汾，具獄辭言惇謀反，景汾率眾擊殺之。

translations.literal: Bolin, honoring Jingfen's righteousness, prepared the case stating that Dun had plotted rebellion and that Jingfen had led the crowd in killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by Jingfen's cause, Bolin drafted the case to say that Dun had plotted rebellion and that Jingfen had led the people in killing him.

sentences.zh: 大吏覆讞惇謀反事無有，乃坐景汾擅殺，伯麟意出入人罪，皆論死。

translations.literal: Superior officials reviewing the case found no evidence that Dun had plotted rebellion; they therefore convicted Jingfen of unauthorized killing and Bolin of intentional distortion in a capital case—both were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Higher officials reviewed the case and found no proof of rebellion. They convicted Jingfen of murder and Bolin of deliberately distorting a capital case. Both were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 逾年遇赦，減死，戍福建。

translations.literal: The next year an amnesty was granted; the death sentences were commuted and Jingfen was exiled to guard Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an amnesty reduced the sentences. Jingfen was sent to garrison duty in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠反，官景汾，事定，逮京師，以從逆見法。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Jingfen was given an official post; when the rebellion was suppressed he was brought to the capital and executed for joining the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Jingfen accepted office under him. After the rebellion was crushed he was taken to the capital and executed as a rebel.

sentences.zh: 僕自聞喜走京師，為具斂。

translations.literal: The servant ran from Wenxi to the capital to prepare his burial.
translations.idiomatic: The servant ran from Wenxi to the capital to lay out Jingfen's body for burial.

sentences.zh: 惇子訐僕不當收罪人屍，下刑部，僕言：「某負三歲主艱難萬死中，辱以義被旌。

translations.literal: Dun's son denounced the servant for improperly receiving a convict's corpse; the case went to the Board of Punishments. The servant said: "I carried my three-year-old master through countless perils; I was honored with commendation for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's son accused the servant of unlawfully claiming a criminal's corpse. The case went to the Board of Punishments. The servant said, "I carried my three-year-old master through a thousand deaths. The court once honored me for loyalty.

sentences.zh: 景汾雖被罪死，固某主也。

translations.literal: Though Jingfen was condemned and died, he was nevertheless my master.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfen was condemned and executed, but he was still my master.

sentences.zh: 主死，僕不為之收，是為無義。

translations.literal: When one's master dies, if a servant does not recover his body, that is unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: When a master dies, a servant who will not recover his body has no honor.

sentences.zh: 某原死，不敢負前旌。」

translations.literal: I am willing to die rather than betray the earlier commendation."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die than disgrace the commendation I once received."

sentences.zh: 獄上，聖祖哀而宥之。

translations.literal: When the case reached the throne, the Kangxi Emperor took pity and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When the case reached the throne, the Kangxi Emperor was moved and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 當精忠官景汾。

translations.literal: When Jingzhong gave Jingfen an official post,
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhong appointed Jingfen to office,

sentences.zh: 亦欲官伯麟，景汾言：「是不辦一縣令，何能為？」

translations.literal: he also wished to give Bolin a post; Jingfen said: "This man cannot even manage a county magistrate—what can he do?"
translations.idiomatic: he also tried to appoint Bolin. Jingfen said, "That man couldn't even run a county—what good would he be?"

sentences.zh: 遂不用，以是免。

translations.literal: So Bolin was not appointed, and thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Bolin was passed over and so escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 胡穆孟，福建人，失其縣。

translations.literal: Hu Mumu, a native of Fujian; his county of origin is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Mumu was from Fujian; his home county is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 順治間武舉。

translations.literal: He was a military licentiate during the Shunzhi reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the military examinations during the Shunzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 與連江沈廷棟同歲，相善。

translations.literal: He was the same year as Shen Tingdong of Lianjiang; the two were close friends.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shen Tingdong of Lianjiang passed in the same year and were close friends.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠反，徵穆孟，避匿廷棟家。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Mumu was summoned; he hid at Tingdong's home.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Mumu was called to serve. He hid in Tingdong's house.

sentences.zh: 廷棟寓書於其友，詆精忠，穆孟竊見之，慮書發且得禍，易書為隱語，邏者得書，猶以詆精忠見收。

translations.literal: Tingdong sent a letter to a friend denouncing Jingzhong; Mumu secretly saw it, fearing that if the letter were discovered disaster would follow, and changed the letter to coded language; the messenger who returned with the letter was still arrested for denouncing Jingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong wrote a friend a letter denouncing Jingzhong. Mumu saw it in secret and, fearing discovery would bring ruin, rewrote it in cipher. Even so, the messenger who carried the letter back was arrested for slandering Jingzhong.

sentences.zh: 穆孟以語其妻王，王謂當自承以脫廷棟。

translations.literal: Mumu told his wife Wang; Wang said she should confess herself to clear Tingdong.
translations.idiomatic: Mumu told his wife Wang. She said she should confess in his place to save Tingdong.

sentences.zh: 穆孟乃詣吏，吏使與廷棟各具書，辨其跡，釋廷棟而殺穆孟。

translations.literal: Mumu then went to the officials; they had him and Tingdong each write out the letter to compare handwriting, released Tingdong, and executed Mumu.
translations.idiomatic: Mumu went to the authorities. They had him and Tingdong each copy the letter to compare handwriting, freed Tingdong, and executed Mumu.

sentences.zh: 穆孟死，王詣市，綴穆孟首，具衣冠為斂，囑子於其叔，且及廷棟，遂縊於屍側，市人皆感泣。

translations.literal: After Mumu died, Wang went to the execution ground, stitched Mumu's head to his body, dressed him in full attire for burial, entrusted her son to his uncle with instructions concerning Tingdong as well, then hanged herself beside the corpse; market-goers all wept.
translations.idiomatic: After Mumu's death Wang went to the execution ground, sewed his head to his body, dressed him for burial, entrusted her son to his uncle with a word for Tingdong, and hanged herself beside the corpse. Everyone in the market wept.

sentences.zh: 師克福建，卹穆孟，廕其子焉。

translations.literal: When the army conquered Fujian, Mumu was posthumously honored and his son granted hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: After Fujian was recovered, the court honored Mumu posthumously and granted hereditary privilege to his son.

sentences.zh: 苑亮，江南亳州人。

translations.literal: Yuan Liang was a native of Bozhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Liang was from Bozhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 事州人韓斌為僕。

translations.literal: He served Han Bin of the prefecture as a servant.
translations.idiomatic: He served Han Bin, a man of the prefecture, as a household servant.

sentences.zh: 斌舉武科，授福建興化守備。

translations.literal: Bin passed the military examinations and was appointed garrison commander of Xinghua in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Han Bin passed the military examination and was appointed garrison commander of Xinghua in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠反，脅授副將，浙江總督李之芳討焉。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Bin was coerced into accepting the rank of vice general; Zhejiang Governor Li Zhifang marched against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Bin was forced to accept the rank of vice general. Zhejiang Governor Li Zhifang marched to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 移江南，錄斌子世晉。

translations.literal: Li moved to Jiangnan and took Bin's son Shi Jin into custody.
translations.idiomatic: Li shifted operations to Jiangnan and detained Bin's son Shi Jin.

sentences.zh: 亮從之行，之芳授以札，使招斌。

translations.literal: Liang accompanied him; Zhifang gave him a letter and sent him to summon Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Liang went with them. Zhifang gave him a letter and sent him to win Bin over.

sentences.zh: 亮度精忠兵所置堠，為邏者所執。

translations.literal: Liang passed through Jingzhong's outposts and was seized by scouts.
translations.idiomatic: Liang passed through Jingzhong's outposts and was caught by scouts.

sentences.zh: 問誰何，亮自陳，言斌家被籍，南來投斌。

translations.literal: Asked who he was, Liang declared himself, saying Bin's household had been confiscated and he had come south to join Bin.
translations.idiomatic: When questioned, Liang gave his name and said Bin's property had been seized and he had come south to join his master.

sentences.zh: 主者監亮見斌，而不許交語。

translations.literal: The officer in charge supervised Liang's meeting with Bin but did not permit them to speak.
translations.idiomatic: The officer in charge brought Liang before Bin under guard but would not let them speak.

sentences.zh: 亮偽遺履，斌發視，得之芳札，乃單騎詣之芳降。

translations.literal: Liang pretended to drop a shoe; Bin opened it and found Zhifang's letter, then rode alone to Zhifang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liang pretended to lose a shoe. Bin opened it, found Zhifang's letter inside, and rode alone to Zhifang to surrender.

sentences.zh: 亮陷賊中，被刑訊，終不言齎札事，遂死。

translations.literal: Liang remained trapped among the rebels, was tortured, and never spoke of carrying the letter; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liang remained in rebel hands, was tortured, and never revealed that he had carried the letter. He died.

sentences.zh: 之芳作傳表之。

translations.literal: Zhifang wrote a biography to commemorate him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang wrote a biography to honor him.

sentences.zh: 楊越，初名春華，字友聲，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Yang Yue, originally named Chunhua, style Yousheng, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yue, born Chunhua, style Yousheng, was from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 所居曰安城，因以為號。

translations.literal: His residence was called Ancheng, which he took as his sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at Ancheng and took that name as his sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，慷慨尚俠。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate, generous and devoted to chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate, he was open-handed and devoted to righteous action.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，越友有與張煌言交通者，事發，辭連越，減死，流寧古塔。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi, a friend of Yue's had dealings with Zhang Huangyan; when the matter came out Yue was implicated by testimony, sentenced to reduced death, and exiled to Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign a friend of Yue's had contact with Zhang Huangyan. When the affair broke, testimony implicated Yue. He was sentenced to commuted death and exiled to Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 例僉妻，與其妻範偕行，留老母及二子家居。

translations.literal: By regulation the wife was conscripted with him; he traveled with his wife Fan, leaving his aged mother and two sons at home.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations required his wife to accompany him. He went with Fan and left his aged mother and two sons at home.

sentences.zh: 寧古塔地初闢，嚴寒，民樸魯。

translations.literal: Ningguta's land was newly opened, bitterly cold, and the people were simple and uncouth.
translations.idiomatic: Ningguta was newly settled country, bitterly cold, and the people were plain and rough.

sentences.zh: 越至，伐木構室，壘土石為炕，出餘物易菽粟。

translations.literal: When Yue arrived, he felled trees to build a dwelling, piled earth and stone for a kang, and traded surplus goods for beans and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue arrived he cut timber for a house, built a kang of earth and stone, and traded what he had for beans and grain.

sentences.zh: 民與習，乃教之讀書，明禮教，崇退讓，躬養老撫孤。

translations.literal: As the people grew accustomed to him, he taught them to read, clarified ritual teaching, honored yielding and deference, and personally cared for the aged and comforted orphans.
translations.idiomatic: Once the people knew him, he taught them to read, explained ritual and propriety, urged humility, and himself cared for the old and sheltered orphans.

sentences.zh: 贖入官為奴者，蕭山李兼汝、蘇州書賈硃方初及黔沐氏之裔忠顯、忠禎皆廩焉。

translations.literal: He redeemed those enslaved to the government: Li Jianru of Xiaoshan, the Suzhou bookseller Zhu Fangchu, and Zhongxian and Zhongzhen, descendants of the Mu clan of Qian—all supported at his expense.
translations.idiomatic: He redeemed people sold into government bondage: Li Jianru of Xiaoshan, the Suzhou bookseller Zhu Fangchu, and Zhongxian and Zhongzhen of the Mu clan of Qian—all kept at his expense.
