sentences.zh: 又贖明大學士硃大典孫婦，河南李天然希聲夫婦。

translations.literal: He also redeemed the granddaughter-in-law of Ming Grand Secretary Zhu Dadian, and Li Tianran and Xisheng, a couple from Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He also redeemed the granddaughter-in-law of the Ming Grand Secretary Zhu Dadian, and Li Tianran and Xisheng, a couple from Henan.

sentences.zh: 凡貧不能舉火及婚喪，倡出貲以周，民相助恐後。

translations.literal: Whenever anyone was too poor to cook or to afford weddings or funerals, he took the lead in contributing funds to help, and the people vied to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever someone could not afford food, a wedding, or a funeral, he was first to give and the people rushed to follow.

sentences.zh: 吝，則嗤之，曰：「何以見楊馬法？」

translations.literal: The stingy were mocked with the words: "How will you face Yang Ma-fa?"
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who held back was mocked: "How will you face Yang Ma-fa?"

sentences.zh: 馬法猶言長老，以敬越也。

translations.literal: Ma-fa" meant elder—an honorific for Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ma-fa" meant elder—a title of respect for Yue.

sentences.zh: 母終於家，年餘始聞喪，哀慟，杜門居三年。

translations.literal: His mother died at home; more than a year passed before he heard the news. Grief-stricken, he shut his door and mourned for three years.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died at home. More than a year passed before word reached him. Stricken with grief, he shut his door and mourned for three years.

sentences.zh: 子賓，出塞省越，越初戍年二十四，至是已六十八。

translations.literal: His son Bin went beyond the frontier to visit Yue; Yue had been twenty-four when first exiled, and was now sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin crossed the frontier to visit him. Yue had been twenty-four when exiled; he was now sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 賓還，叩閽乞赦越，事未行。

translations.literal: Bin returned and knocked at the palace gate begging Yue's pardon; the petition did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Bin returned and petitioned at the palace gates for Yue's pardon, but the plea failed.

sentences.zh: 子寶，復出塞省越。

translations.literal: His son Bao again went beyond the frontier to visit Yue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bao crossed the frontier again to visit him.

sentences.zh: 又二年，越卒於戍所，例不得歸葬，賓、寶請不已，又二年乃得請。

translations.literal: Two years later Yue died at his place of exile; by regulation he could not be buried back home. Bin and Bao petitioned unceasingly; only after two more years was permission granted.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Yue died in exile. By rule his body could not be returned. Bin and Bao petitioned without rest until, two years later, permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 迎範奉越喪以歸，民送者哭填路。

translations.literal: They welcomed Fan and brought Yue's coffin home; the people who saw them off wept until the road was filled.
translations.idiomatic: They brought Fan and Yue's coffin home. Those who saw them off wept until the road was crowded with mourners.

sentences.zh: 賓撰柳邊紀略，述塞外事甚詳。

translations.literal: Bin compiled the Brief Account of the Willow Frontier, narrating frontier affairs in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: Bin wrote the Brief Account of the Willow Frontier, describing life beyond the pass in rich detail.

sentences.zh: 吳鴻錫，字允康，福建晉江人。

translations.literal: Wu Hongxi, style Yunkang, was a native of Jinjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Hongxi, style Yunkang, was from Jinjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 父德佑，康熙初，客浙江，兵部郎中噶尼布奉命督造戰艦，延德佑入幕。

translations.literal: His father Deyou, early in Kangxi, was a guest in Zhejiang; Ministry of War Director Gani Bu was ordered to supervise construction of warships and invited Deyou into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: His father Deyou, early in Kangxi, was staying in Zhejiang when Gani Bu of the Ministry of War was ordered to oversee warship construction and took Deyou onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 數月德佑卒，鴻錫方七歲，噶尼布攜至京，將子之，鴻錫請呼以伯，曰：「父一而已。」

translations.literal: Several months later Deyou died; Hongxi was only seven. Gani Bu took him to the capital intending to adopt him as a son; Hongxi asked to call him "uncle," saying: "One has only one father."
translations.idiomatic: A few months later Deyou died. Hongxi was only seven. Gani Bu brought him to the capital and meant to adopt him, but Hongxi asked to call him Uncle, saying, "A man has only one father."

sentences.zh: 噶尼布奇之，曰：「七歲兒能辨此耶？」

translations.literal: Gani Bu marveled at this, saying: "Can a seven-year-old child discern this?"
translations.idiomatic: Gani Bu was astonished. "Can a seven-year-old know that?" he said.

sentences.zh: 噶尼布故廉，家漸困，鴻錫為督芻牧，私市書冊、弓矢習之。

translations.literal: Gani Bu had been upright by nature; his household gradually grew impoverished. Hongxi supervised fodder and herding, privately bought books and bows and arrows and practiced with them.
translations.idiomatic: Gani Bu had lived plainly and his household grew poor. Hongxi oversaw fodder and livestock, and on his own bought books, bows, and arrows and trained with them.

sentences.zh: 通滿、漢文，精騎射。

translations.literal: He was fluent in Manchu and Chinese and skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered both Manchu and Chinese and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 噶尼布從兄雲麟以平台灣功授溫州參將，至京師，欲以鴻錫行，噶尼布諾之。

translations.literal: Gani Bu's cousin Yunlin was appointed Wenzhou brigade commander for service at Pingtai Bay; arriving at the capital, he wished to take Hongxi with him, and Gani Bu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Gani Bu's cousin Yunlin was made Wenzhou brigade commander for his service at Pingtai Bay. When he reached the capital he wanted Hongxi to go with him, and Gani Bu consented.

sentences.zh: 鴻錫流涕曰：「我七歲育於公，今我壯而公老，父子幼，必俟其成立，我乃歸。」

translations.literal: Hongxi wept and said: "I was raised by you from age seven; now I am grown and you are old, with young sons—I must wait until they come of age before I may leave."
translations.idiomatic: Hongxi wept and said, "You raised me from seven. Now I am grown and you are old, with young sons still at home. I cannot leave until they are established."

sentences.zh: 鎮國公海清，噶尼布壻也，義鴻錫俾入旗。

translations.literal: Prince of the State Haising, Gani Bu's son-in-law, honored Hongxi and had him enrolled in the banner.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Haising, Gani Bu's son-in-law, admired Hongxi and had him enrolled in the banner rolls.

sentences.zh: 噶尼布卒，妻哀甚，得狂疾。

translations.literal: When Gani Bu died, his wife grieved deeply and developed a mental disorder.
translations.idiomatic: After Gani Bu died his wife grieved so deeply that she lost her mind.

sentences.zh: 子和順、和鼐、和麟。

translations.literal: She had sons Hesun, Henai, and Helin.
translations.idiomatic: She had three sons: Hesun, Henai, and Helin.

sentences.zh: 和順才七歲，鴻錫為治喪，持家政，延師教和順兄弟，稍長，為娶婦。

translations.literal: Hesun was only seven; Hongxi arranged the funeral, managed the household, hired teachers for Hesun and his brothers, and when they grew older found wives for them.
translations.idiomatic: Hesun was only seven. Hongxi handled the funeral, ran the household, hired tutors for Hesun and his brothers, and when they were older found wives for them.

sentences.zh: 和順年十六，有忌之者，授以護軍，將困苦之。

translations.literal: When Hesun was sixteen, someone who envied him had him appointed a guard soldier, intending to make life hard for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hesun turned sixteen, a jealous man had him posted as a guard soldier, intending to wear him down.

sentences.zh: 每值宿，鴻錫佩刀以從，露坐終夜。

translations.literal: Whenever he was on night duty, Hongxi wore a sword and followed him, sitting in the open all night.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hesun stood night watch, Hongxi girded on a sword and kept him company, sitting in the open until dawn.

sentences.zh: 大學士阿蘭泰為噶尼布故交，鴻錫率和順兄弟候其門，和順試除中書。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Alantai was an old friend of Ganib's; Hongxi led the Hesun brothers to wait at his gate, and Hesun was granted probationary appointment as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Alantai had been Ganib's old friend. Hongxi brought the Hesun brothers to wait at his gate, and Hesun received a probationary appointment as a Grand Secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 師徵噶爾丹，和順從軍，以功擢禮部主事。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Galdan, Hesun followed the campaign and, for merit, was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched against Galdan, Hesun went with it and, for his service, was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 有召和順飲者，佐以博，鴻錫持刀迳入坐以和順歸。

translations.literal: When someone invited Hesun to drink and added gambling, Hongxi drew his knife, walked straight in, and sat there until Hesun went home.
translations.idiomatic: When someone invited Hesun to drink and set out dice beside the wine, Hongxi drew his knife, strode in, and sat there until Hesun came home.

sentences.zh: 他日，或問鴻錫：「人可殺乎？」

translations.literal: Another day someone asked Hongxi: "Can a man be killed?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day someone asked Hongxi, "Would you kill a man?"

sentences.zh: 鴻錫曰：「殺人罪不過死，吾受撫孤託，而坐視其溺於燕朋，誠生不如死。

translations.literal: Hongxi said: "The crime of killing is no more than death. I accepted the charge to raise these orphans, yet sit by watching him drown in carousing companions—for such a life, death would be better.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxi said, "Killing a man is a crime no worse than death. I took on the trust of raising these orphans, yet I sit by while he sinks into dissolute company—for that, death would be better than life.

sentences.zh: 死而諸孤知勉，則死賢於生矣。」

translations.literal: If in dying the orphans learn diligence, then death is better than life."
translations.idiomatic: If my death makes the orphans learn to strive, then dying would be better than living."

sentences.zh: 和順自是不復與人飲。

translations.literal: From then on Hesun never again drank with others.
translations.idiomatic: After that Hesun never drank with others again.

sentences.zh: 山東飢，遣官治賑，和順與焉，鴻錫從之。

translations.literal: Shandong suffered famine; officials were sent to administer relief, and Hesun was among them; Hongxi went with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong fell into famine, officials were sent to organize relief. Hesun was among them, and Hongxi went with him.

sentences.zh: 武城廩未發，出私錢散米，又慮飢者驟飽且致斃，瀹萊菔飲之，全活無算。

translations.literal: The Wucheng granary had not yet opened its stores; he spent private money to distribute rice; fearing that the hungry, if suddenly sated, might die from it, he boiled radish for them to drink—countless lives were saved.
translations.idiomatic: The Wucheng granary had not yet opened its stores, so he spent his own money to give out rice. Fearing that the starving, if suddenly filled, might die from it, he boiled radish for them to drink with it—and saved lives beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 和順尋榷密雲關，鴻錫曰：「負販小民不得取其稅，額不足，可以家財補焉。」

translations.literal: Hesun soon took charge of the Miyun Pass levy; Hongxi said: "Small peddlers must not be taxed; if the quota falls short, household wealth can make up the difference."
translations.idiomatic: Hesun was soon put in charge of the levy at Miyun Pass. Hongxi said, "Do not take tax from petty peddlers. If the quota falls short, make it up from our household funds."

sentences.zh: 民歡趨之，額亦足。

translations.literal: The people came gladly, and the quota was also filled.
translations.idiomatic: The people came gladly, and the quota was met as well.

sentences.zh: 和鼐習舉業，鴻錫督之，慮其怠，穴幾貫鐵索自系守之，和鼐驚謝，讀益力，以副榜貢生得官。

translations.literal: Henai studied for the examinations; Hongxi supervised him, fearing idleness; he bored a hole in the desk, threaded an iron chain through, and tethered himself to guard him. Henai was startled and apologized, read all the harder, and gained office as a tribute student on the alternate list.
translations.idiomatic: Henai prepared for the civil examinations under Hongxi's supervision. Fearing slackness, Hongxi bored a hole in the desk, ran an iron chain through it, and tethered himself there to keep watch. Henai was startled and apologized, studied all the harder, and eventually gained office as a tribute student on the alternate list.

sentences.zh: 和麟年十六，鴻錫偕詣永定河效力，水大至，巡撫於成龍夜行堤上，見有向河拜且泣者，問之，鴻錫也，解衣旌之。

translations.literal: When Helin was sixteen, Hongxi went with him to work on the Yongding River. Great floods came. Governor Yu Chenglong walked the dike at night and saw someone bowing toward the river and weeping; on inquiry it was Hongxi; he removed his robe to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: When Helin was sixteen, Hongxi went with him to labor on the Yongding River. The waters rose in flood. Governor Yu Chenglong walked the dike by night and saw someone bowing toward the river and weeping. Asked who it was, he learned it was Hongxi and removed his own robe to honor him.

sentences.zh: 工竟，和麟議敘筆帖式，擢刑部郎中。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, Helin was recommended for evaluation as a clerk and promoted to director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done, Helin was recommended for clerk's evaluation and promoted to director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 鴻錫不得歸，募工寫父母遺像，檢父遺衣冠招魂葬之。

translations.literal: Hongxi could not return home; he hired artisans to paint portraits of his deceased parents and gathered his father's remaining clothes for a soul-invoking burial.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to return home, Hongxi hired artisans to paint portraits of his dead parents, gathered his father's remaining garments, and buried them in a soul-invoking rite.

sentences.zh: 年五十八，卒。

translations.literal: At age fifty-eight, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 和順兄弟去纓席地，如父母喪。

translations.literal: The Hesun brothers removed their official tassels and sat on the ground, as for parents in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Hesun brothers removed their official tassels and sat on the bare ground, mourning him as they would a parent.

sentences.zh: 韓瑜，字玉採，山東濰縣人。

translations.literal: Han Yu, style name Yucai, was a native of Weixian in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, styled Yucai, was from Weixian in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his mother filially.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he served his mother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 母歿，哭泣三年。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he wept for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he mourned and wept for three years.

sentences.zh: 既除喪，祭墓未嘗不哀，年八十如故。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, whenever he sacrificed at her tomb he was never without grief; at eighty he was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ended, he never visited her tomb without grief, and at eighty he was the same as ever.

sentences.zh: 冠時母有衣一襲，★M8篋中，賓祭則服之，衣敝不棄。

translations.literal: When he came of age his mother had left him a suit of clothes stored in a chest; at guest sacrifices he wore them; though worn he never discarded them.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age his mother had left him a suit of clothes stored in a chest. He wore them at sacrifices for guests, and though they were worn threadbare he never cast them aside.

sentences.zh: 將卒，命以斂，猶舉孟郊詩曰：「此慈母手中線也。」

translations.literal: Near death, he ordered them used for his encoffinment, and still quoted Meng Jiao's poem: "These are threads from a loving mother's hand."
translations.idiomatic: As death approached, he ordered those clothes used to shroud him, and still quoted Meng Jiao's line: "These are threads from a loving mother's hand."

sentences.zh: 事兄謹，兄弟皆八十，無改常度。

translations.literal: He served his elder brother respectfully; the brothers all reached eighty without changing their usual conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He served his elder brother with care. The brothers all lived to eighty without altering their usual ways.

sentences.zh: 產不過中人，好施予，多蓄書，遇寒士則遺之。

translations.literal: His property was no more than middle-class; he loved giving, kept many books, and when he met poor scholars he would give them away.
translations.idiomatic: His means were no more than comfortable middle rank, yet he loved to give. He kept many books and, when he met poor scholars, would make gifts of them.

sentences.zh: 族黨長不能婚娶，喪不能葬，必佽以貲。

translations.literal: When kinsmen grown old could not marry, or could not bury their dead, he always loaned them funds.
translations.idiomatic: When clansmen too old to marry on their own lacked the means, or when families could not afford burial, he always lent them money.

sentences.zh: 族子貧，贈以秫十石，使居賈。

translations.literal: A clansman's son was poor; he gave him ten shi of sorghum and had him set up as a merchant.
translations.idiomatic: When a clansman's son was poor, he gave him ten shi of sorghum and set him up in trade.

sentences.zh: 得贏，倍以償，不受。

translations.literal: When he profited, he tried to repay double; Han Yu would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the boy turned a profit, he tried to repay double. Han Yu would not take it.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十三年，飢，民鬻子女，罄所蓄，得九人，不立券。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Kangxi, famine struck; people sold their children; he emptied his savings and redeemed nine persons, without written bonds.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 43 famine struck and people sold their children. Han Yu spent all he had saved and redeemed nine of them, without so much as a written bond.

sentences.zh: 歲豐，悉遣還之。

translations.literal: When the year was bountiful, he sent them all back.
translations.idiomatic: When the harvest was good again, he sent them all back to their families.

sentences.zh: 卒時八十有六。

translations.literal: At death he was eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 程增，字維高，江南歙縣人。

translations.literal: Cheng Zeng, style name Weigao, was a native of Shexian in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zeng, styled Weigao, was from Shexian in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父朝聘，自歙移家安東。

translations.literal: His father Chaopin moved the family from She to Andong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chaopin had moved the family from She to Andong.

sentences.zh: 歸省墓，病作。

translations.literal: Zeng returned to visit the tomb and his father fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng returned home to tend the tombs, and his father fell ill.

sentences.zh: 增冒風渡江，六日夜行千五百里，至則朝聘已歿。

translations.literal: Zeng braved the wind to cross the river; six days and nights of travel covering one thousand five hundred li—when he arrived Chaopin had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng braved wind and cold to cross the river, traveling day and night for six days over fifteen hundred li—and arrived to find Chaopin already dead.

sentences.zh: 母唐病復作，急還，又已歿，乃絕意仕進。

translations.literal: His mother Tang's illness recurred; he hurried back, but she too had died; he then abandoned all thought of an official career.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Tang's illness returned. He hurried back, only to find her dead as well, and from then on gave up all thought of an official career.

sentences.zh: 安東地卑，母柩在堂，水大至，增與一僕力升柩木案上。

translations.literal: Andong's land was low; his mother's coffin was in the hall; great floods came; Zeng and one servant strained to lift the coffin onto a wooden platform.
translations.idiomatic: Andong lay low, and his mother's coffin still rested in the hall when great floods came. Zeng and a single servant strained to raise the coffin onto a wooden platform.

sentences.zh: 既葬，复移家山陽為賈，而使二弟就學。

translations.literal: After burial, he again moved the family to Shanyang to trade, and had his two younger brothers pursue study.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he moved the family again to Shanyang to trade, and sent his two younger brothers to study.

sentences.zh: 父母之黨死而無歸者畢葬焉，餘皆定其居，使有恆業。

translations.literal: All relatives of his parents who died with no one to bring them home he buried completely; the rest he settled in fixed residences and gave them steady livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He buried every kinsman of his parents who died far from home with no one to bring them back, and for the rest he found fixed dwellings and steady livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 析田立塾，以養以教。

translations.literal: He divided fields to establish a school, for nurture and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside fields to endow a school, providing both support and instruction.

sentences.zh: 友有急難，以千金脫之，後更相背，窮復來自解，待之如初。

translations.literal: A friend in urgent distress—he lent a thousand gold to free him; later they turned against each other; when poor he came to explain himself; Zeng treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: When a friend fell into desperate trouble, he lent a thousand in gold to free him. Later they quarreled and parted; when the man was poor again he came to explain himself, and Zeng treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，河、淮溢，增出家財修邗溝兩岸堤十里，河道總督張鵬翮以聞。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi, the Yellow and Huai rivers overflowed; Zeng spent household wealth to repair ten li of dikes on both banks of the Hangou canal; Grand Canal Governor Zhang Penghe reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign the Yellow and Huai rivers burst their banks. Zeng spent his household fortune repairing ten li of dikes on both banks of the Hangou canal, and Grand Canal Governor Zhang Penghe reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十四年，聖祖巡視芒稻河，召增入見，書「旌勞」二字以賜。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Kangxi, the Sage Emperor inspected the Mangdao River, summoned Zeng for audience, and wrote the two characters "Commend Labor" to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 44 the Sage Emperor inspected the Mangdao River, summoned Zeng to audience, and wrote the two characters "Commend Labor" as a gift.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督於成龍好微行，奸人因造言傾怨家，獄或失入。

translations.literal: Liangjiang Governor Yu Chenglong liked to travel incognito; scoundrels therefore spread rumors to ruin those they hated, and cases sometimes wrongly imprisoned people.
translations.idiomatic: Liangjiang Governor Yu Chenglong liked to travel incognito. Scoundrels therefore spread slander to ruin their enemies, and innocent people were sometimes wrongly imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 增謁成龍，力言其弊，指事為徵，成龍曰：「微子言，吾安知人心抗敝至此！」

translations.literal: Zeng visited Yu Chenglong and spoke forcefully of this abuse, citing concrete cases as proof; Yu Chenglong said: "But for your words, how would I know hearts are so resistant and corrupt!"
translations.idiomatic: Zeng visited Yu Chenglong and spoke bluntly of the abuse, citing specific cases as proof. Yu Chenglong said, "Had you not spoken, how would I have known that hearts had grown so stubborn and corrupt!"

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Many years later he died.

sentences.zh: 李應卜，河南郟縣人。

translations.literal: Li Yingbu was a native of Jia County in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yingbu was from Jia County in Henan.

sentences.zh: 早失父母，叔丕基遺側室，事如母，壽百歲終。

translations.literal: He lost his parents early; his uncle Piji left a concubine; he served her as a mother; she lived to a hundred and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents early. His uncle Piji left behind a concubine, whom he served as a mother; she lived to a hundred and died.

sentences.zh: 侄緯，孤，飲食教誨之。

translations.literal: His nephew Wei was orphaned; he fed, taught, and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Wei was orphaned, and he fed, taught, and raised him.

sentences.zh: 病作，必數視之，曰：「我夜不能起，然終宵未成寢也！」

translations.literal: When illness arose he always visited repeatedly, saying: "I cannot rise at night, yet all night I never truly sleep!"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wei fell ill, he visited again and again, saying, "I cannot get up at night, yet I never truly sleep through the night!"

sentences.zh: 弟應會亡，病甚，一夕鬚​​髮皆白​​。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yinghui died; his illness was severe; in one night his beard and hair all turned white.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother Yinghui died, grief laid him so low that in a single night his beard and hair turned white.

sentences.zh: 侄緝幼，食必呼共案，出必視而行，返必問在何所。

translations.literal: His nephew Ji was young; at meals he always called him to share the table; going out he watched him leave; returning he asked where he had been.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Ji was still young. At meals he always called the boy to share his table; when Ji went out he watched him go; when he returned he asked where he had been.

sentences.zh: 施及於鄉人，有典其田而遠遊者，以子託焉，久之，為娶婦，且復其田。

translations.literal: His generosity extended to villagers: someone had pawned his fields and gone far to travel, entrusting his son to Yingbu; after a long time he found him a wife and also restored his fields.
translations.idiomatic: His kindness reached the village as well. One man had pawned his fields and gone far away, leaving his son in Yingbu's care. In time Yingbu found the boy a wife and restored his fields besides.

sentences.zh: 有喪其妻者，為之复娶，予田，俾資以生。

translations.literal: When someone lost his wife, he found him another wife, gave him fields, so he could support himself.
translations.idiomatic: When a man lost his wife, he found him another and gave him fields so he could live.

sentences.zh: 有貧欲遠徙者，予之粟，留勿徙。

translations.literal: When someone poor wished to migrate far, he gave him grain and persuaded him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: When a poor man meant to move far away, he gave him grain and persuaded him to stay.

sentences.zh: 有傭於其肆，負金，病且死者，為之蠲其逋，厚給其妻子。

translations.literal: Someone hired at his shop owed money, was sick and near death; he cancelled the debt and generously provided for his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: A hired man in his shop owed him money and lay sick near death. Yingbu cancelled the debt and gave generously to the man's wife and children.

sentences.zh: 有持金入其肆市粟者，視金有官封，與粟，遣之去。

translations.literal: Someone brought gold into his shop to buy grain; seeing the gold bore an official seal, he gave grain and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Once a man brought gold into his shop to buy grain. Seeing that the gold bore an official seal, Yingbu gave him the grain and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 持金詣縣庭，知縣方以庫失金笞吏，應卜以金上，具言始末，事乃白。

translations.literal: The man took the gold to the county yamen; the magistrate was just beating a clerk for lost treasury gold; Yingbu presented the gold and explained the whole course of events; the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The man took the gold to the county yamen just as the magistrate was flogging a clerk over missing treasury gold. Yingbu brought forward the gold and explained the whole affair, and the matter was cleared.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，縣舉應卜行事上大吏，請旌表其門曰「義士」。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, the county reported Yingbu's conduct to higher officials and requested an inscribed commendation for his gate reading "Righteous Man."
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 the county reported Yingbu's deeds to higher officials and asked that his gate be inscribed with the title "Righteous Man."

sentences.zh: 塞勒，滿洲人。

translations.literal: Saile was a Manchu.
translations.idiomatic: Saile was a Manchu.

sentences.zh: 官苑副。

translations.literal: He held the post of deputy superintendent of the imperial gardens.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy superintendent of the imperial gardens.

sentences.zh: 與惠色友，塞勒老無子，時引以為戚。

translations.literal: He was friends with Huise; Saile grew old without sons and often took this as sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: He was friends with Huise. Saile grew old childless and often grieved over it.

sentences.zh: 惠色曰：「我已有二子，今婦又有身，男也，為君子。」

translations.literal: Huise said: "I already have two sons; now my wife is again with child—a boy—I give him to you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: Huise said, "I already have two sons, and now my wife is with child again. If it is a boy, he is yours, sir."

sentences.zh: 已而得男，命曰奇豐額。

translations.literal: Soon a boy was born; he was named Qifenge.
translations.idiomatic: A boy was born, and Huise named him Qifenge.

sentences.zh: 既免乳，以畀塞勒，塞勒與其妻撫以為子。

translations.literal: Once weaned from the breast, he was given to Saile; Saile and his wife raised him as their son.
translations.idiomatic: Once the boy was weaned, Huise gave him to Saile, and Saile and his wife raised him as their own son.

sentences.zh: 年十六，將應童子試，當具三代，塞勒曰：「吾寧無子，不可改祖宗，欺君父！」

translations.literal: At sixteen, about to take the child examination, one must declare three generations; Saile said: "I would rather be without a son than alter my ancestors and deceive lord and father!"
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, when Qifenge was about to sit for the child examination and had to declare three generations of ancestry, Saile said, "I would rather have no son than falsify my ancestors and deceive my lord and father!"

sentences.zh: 乃攜奇豐額還惠色。

translations.literal: He then took Qifenge back to Huise.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Qifenge back to Huise.

sentences.zh: 奇豐額初不自知惠色子，塞勒語以故，駷馬去。

translations.literal: Qifenge at first did not know he was Huise's son; Saile told him the reason; he galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: Qifenge had not known he was Huise's son. When Saile told him why, he mounted and galloped away.

sentences.zh: 奇豐額遂還為惠色子，乾隆三十四年成進士，授刑部主事，累遷江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: Qifenge then returned to be Huise's son; in the thirty-fourth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, and rose cumulatively to Jiangsu provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Qifenge then returned to Huise's household. In Qianlong 34 he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, and rose step by step to Jiangsu provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 塞勒及其妻相繼卒。

translations.literal: Saile and his wife died in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Saile and his wife died one after another.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，奇豐額擢江蘇巡撫，入覲，涕泣陳本末，請以本身封典貤封塞勒，並以第三子廣麟為塞勒後。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year, Qifenge was promoted to Jiangsu governor; entering audience he wept and stated the whole story, requesting to use his own rank honors to posthumously ennoble Saile by extension, and to make his third son Guanglin Saile's heir.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 57 Qifenge was promoted to governor of Jiangsu. At audience he wept and told the whole story, asking to extend his own honors posthumously to Saile and to make his third son Guanglin Saile's heir.

sentences.zh: 上命具疏，下部議，皆不許，上特允之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered a memorial prepared; it went to the ministry for deliberation; all denied it; the Emperor specially approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered a memorial drawn up and sent it to the ministries for deliberation. All recommended refusal, but the Emperor granted it by special decree.

sentences.zh: 奇豐額，黃氏，先世朝鮮人，隸內務府滿洲正白旗。

translations.literal: Qifenge, surname Huang; his forebears were Koreans; he belonged to the Manchu Plain White Banner of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Qifenge, of the Huang clan, was descended from Koreans and belonged to the Manchu Plain White Banner of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 坐事罷官，終內務府主事。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office for an offense and ended as a chief clerk of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed from office for an offense, he ended his career as a chief clerk of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 王聯，字鷺亭，江蘇泰州人。

translations.literal: Wang Lian, style name Luting, was a native of Taizhou in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lian, styled Luting, was from Taizhou in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 應乾隆四十五年江南鄉試，聯與友沈某偕。

translations.literal: For the Jiangnan provincial examination of Qianlong 45, Lian went together with a friend surnamed Shen.
translations.idiomatic: For the Jiangnan provincial examination of Qianlong 45, Lian set out with a friend surnamed Shen.

sentences.zh: 沈病於喉，欲歸，聯不入試，送之還。

translations.literal: Shen had a throat ailment and wished to return; Lian did not enter the examination but escorted him home.
translations.idiomatic: Shen had a throat ailment and wanted to turn back. Lian did not sit for the examination but escorted him home instead.

sentences.zh: 至龍潭，沈病益劇，聯伴之寢，病者口腐，穢觸鼻，不問。

translations.literal: At Longtan, Shen's illness grew worse; Lian slept beside him; the sick man's mouth rotted and the stench reached his nose—he did not mind.
translations.idiomatic: At Longtan Shen's illness worsened. Lian slept beside him; the sick man's mouth festered and the stench filled his nostrils, yet he did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 輿行慮其顛，徒步翼以行。

translations.literal: When traveling by sedan he feared Shen would be jolted; he walked on foot to flank and steady the procession.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the sedan would jolt Shen, he walked on foot beside it to steady the bearers.

sentences.zh: 沈遽死，輿者欲散，聯以義感之，乃得至丹徒，殯於僧寺，以其柩歸。

translations.literal: Shen suddenly died; the bearers wished to disperse; Lian moved them by righteousness and so reached Dantu, coffined him at a monastery, and brought the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: Shen died suddenly. The bearers meant to scatter, but Lian moved them by his example and so reached Dantu, laid the body in a coffin at a monastery, and brought the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 論者謂新唐書以張道源送友屍歸里，列諸忠義傳，聯亦其亞也。

translations.literal: Commentators say the New Tang History lists Zhang Daoyuan for returning a friend's corpse to his homeland in the Loyalty and Righteousness biographies—Lian is nearly his equal.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators observed that the New Tang History placed Zhang Daoyuan in the biographies of loyalty and righteousness for returning a friend's corpse to his homeland—and that Lian was scarcely his inferior.

sentences.zh: 黎侗，安南人，故安南國王黎維祁之族也。

translations.literal: Li Tong was an Annamese, a kinsman of the former king of Annam, Li Weishi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong was an Annamese and a kinsman of the former king of Annam, Li Weishi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，廣南阮光平破安南，侗護維祁叩關乞援，上遣孫士毅率師送歸國。

translations.literal: During Qianlong, Guangnan's Ruan Guangping destroyed Annam; Tong escorted Weishi to the border to beg aid; the Emperor sent Sun Shiyi at the head of an army to restore him to his kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong reign Ruan Guangping of Guangnan overthrew Annam. Tong escorted Weishi to the frontier to beg aid, and the Emperor sent Sun Shiyi at the head of an army to restore him to his throne.

sentences.zh: 既，復為光平襲破，維祁出走，侗齎上所賜國王印走，間道入關，與段旺等二十九人俱。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Weishi was again attacked and defeated by Guangping; Weishi fled; Tong carried the king's seal bestowed by the court and fled by secret paths into the frontier, together with Duan Wang and twenty-nine others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Guangping struck again and Weishi fled. Tong took the king's seal bestowed by the court and, with Duan Wang and twenty-nine others, made his way by hidden routes back into China.

sentences.zh: 上命薙發，分置江、浙諸地，獨侗與李秉道等四人不肯從。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered them to shave their heads and be settled in Jiangsu and Zhejiang; only Tong and Li Bingdao among four refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered them shaved and resettled across Jiangsu and Zhejiang. Of the four who refused, Tong and Li Bingdao were two.

sentences.zh: 其一為黎駟，亦維祁族，其一失姓名，四人者堅請得出關為維祁復仇。

translations.literal: One was Li Si, also of Weishi's clan; one has lost his name; the four strongly petitioned to be allowed to leave the frontier to avenge Weishi.
translations.idiomatic: One was Li Si, also of Weishi's clan; one man's name is lost. All four pleaded insistently to be allowed out of the frontier to avenge Weishi.

sentences.zh: 上已受光平降，不欲更為黎氏出兵。

translations.literal: The Emperor had already accepted Guangping's surrender and did not wish to send troops again for the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had already accepted Guangping's surrender and had no wish to send troops again on behalf of the Li.

sentences.zh: 謂侗等忠於黎氏，不以盛衰為去就，諭福康安平心詢問。

translations.literal: Saying Tong and the others were loyal to the Li without regard to fortune or decline, he instructed Fuk'anggan to inquire with an even mind.
translations.idiomatic: Calling Tong and his companions loyal to the Li regardless of fortune or ruin, he instructed Fuk'anggan to question them fairly.

sentences.zh: 士毅尋奏：「侗假託忠義，意圖構釁。」

translations.literal: Shiyi soon memorialized: "Tong feigns loyalty and righteousness, intending to provoke conflict."
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi soon memorialized, "Tong feigns loyalty and righteousness, intending to stir up trouble."

sentences.zh: 上命侗等從維祁至京師，令軍機大臣傳詢。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Tong and the others to follow Weishi to the capital and had the Grand Council ministers conduct inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Tong and the others to accompany Weishi to the capital and had the Grand Council ministers examine them.

sentences.zh: 侗等力請還黎氏故土，誓以死殉。

translations.literal: Tong and the others strongly petitioned to return to Li territory and swore to die for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Tong and the others pleaded to return to Li territory and swore to die for the cause.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「侗等仍還安南，或為光平所戮，朕心所不忍。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If Tong and the others returned to Annam, they might be executed by Guangping—what my heart cannot bear."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "If Tong and his companions returned to Annam, Guangping might kill them—and that my heart cannot bear."

sentences.zh: 命暫系刑部獄。

translations.literal: He ordered them temporarily imprisoned in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them held for the time being in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 維祁卒，葬京師郊外。

translations.literal: Weishi died and was buried outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiqi died he was buried in the suburbs of the capital.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，命釋四人者，使居外火器營。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jiaqing ascended, he ordered the four released and had them live at the Outer Firearms Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiaqing ascended the throne, he ordered the four released and settled them at the Outer Firearms Brigade.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶八年，農耐阮福映並安南，使上表乞封，侗子光倬在行，侗與秉道至涿州迓焉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiaqing, Nongnai's Ruan Fouying united Annam and sent an envoy to petition for investiture; Tong's son Guangzhuo was in the entourage; Tong and Bingdao went to Zhuozhou to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 8 Ruan Fouying of Nongnai united Annam and sent an envoy to petition for investiture. Tong's son Guangzhuo was in the embassy, and Tong and Bingdao went to Zhuozhou to meet them.

sentences.zh: 仁宗責其私出，下刑部。

translations.literal: Emperor Jiaqing rebuked them for going out privately and referred the matter to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiaqing rebuked them for leaving without permission and referred the matter to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 侗等初自承出謁維祁墓，既乃具言原得歸國，並以維祁喪還葬。

translations.literal: Tong and the others had first come forward of their own accord to visit Weiqi's tomb; afterward they set forth in full that they wished to return to their country, and also to bring Weiqi's remains back for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Tong and his companions, having come forward on their own to pay respects at Weiqi's tomb, then explained in full their wish to return home and to bring Weiqi's remains back for burial.

sentences.zh: 上許之，賚以銀，並諸黎氏舊臣入漢軍置內地者悉遣還。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it, bestowed silver, and also sent back all the former ministers of the Li clan who had been enrolled in the Han Banner and settled in the interior.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted their request, rewarded them with silver, and ordered every former Li minister who had been placed in the Han Banner and resettled inland sent home.

sentences.zh: 趙瓏，字雨亭，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Zhao Long, courtesy name Yuting, was a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Long, styled Yuting, was from Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 倜儻重然諾。

translations.literal: He was free-spirited and valued his word above all.
translations.idiomatic: He was unconventional in spirit and held his pledges sacred.

sentences.zh: 有葉暘者，與有連，官大名同知，瓏往客焉。

translations.literal: There was one Ye Yang, related to him by marriage, who served as vice-prefect of Daming; Long went to stay with him as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman by marriage, Ye Yang, held the post of vice-prefect at Daming; Long went to lodge with him.

sentences.zh: 甫踰月，暘坐事戍伊犁，僮僕皆散走，暘父母老且病，日夜泣，瓏請與俱行。

translations.literal: Scarcely a month later, Yang was convicted and banished to Ili; servants and attendants all scattered and fled. Yang's parents were old and ill, weeping day and night; Long asked to go with them.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month passed before Yang was convicted and sent to exile in Ili. Servants and attendants fled in every direction, while Yang's aged, ailing parents wept without cease. Long asked to accompany them.

sentences.zh: 既至，將軍愛暘才，置幕中，瓏乃辭歸。

translations.literal: Once they arrived, the general admired Yang's talent and placed him on his staff; Long then took leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, the general admired Yang's abilities and took him onto his staff. Long then bowed out and went home.

sentences.zh: 暘泣，瓏曰：「勿爾！

translations.literal: Yang wept. Long said, "Do not be like that! I shall come again."
translations.idiomatic: Yang wept. Long said, "Enough of that—I shall come again."

sentences.zh: 吾且再來。」

translations.literal: A year after he returned home, Yang's mother died, and Long went again.
translations.idiomatic: A year after his return, Yang's mother died, and Long set out once more.

sentences.zh: 歸一年，暘母卒，瓏復往。

translations.literal: As he was crossing the frontier pass, he heard that Yang had moved with the general to a new posting at Tarbagatai; he changed route and went there.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was leaving the pass, he learned that Yang had moved with the general to Tarbagatai. He changed course and went there instead.

sentences.zh: 比出關，聞暘從將軍移駐塔爾巴哈台，改途赴之。

translations.literal: When the general heard of it, he esteemed Long and called him "a man of righteousness," and from this Zhao the Righteous Man's name became famous beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The general, hearing of it, honored Long and called him "a man of righteousness." From that day the name of Zhao the Righteous Man rang across the frontier.

sentences.zh: 將軍聞，賢瓏，稱曰「義士」，以此趙義士名著關外。

translations.literal: There was one Ye Chun, of Yang's clan, who was also banished to Ili.
translations.idiomatic: Another clansman of Yang's, Ye Chun, was also serving exile in Ili.

sentences.zh: 有葉椿者，暘同族也，亦戍伊犁。

translations.literal: When Long set out across the pass again, Chun's mother attached to him a letter for her son and sent money.
translations.idiomatic: When Long crossed the frontier again, Chun's mother entrusted him with a letter for her son and a sum of money.

sentences.zh: 瓏再出關，椿母附寄子書致金。

translations.literal: Long had already changed course for Tarbagatai and did not reach Ili.
translations.idiomatic: Long had already diverted toward Tarbagatai and never reached Ili.

sentences.zh: 瓏既改赴塔爾巴哈台，未至伊犁。

translations.literal: On the road back at Hutubi he met the patrol inspector Chen Shi, also a man of Anhui; when he traced Chun, he found Chun had long been dead.
translations.idiomatic: On the return road at Hutubi he met the patrol inspector Chen Shi, a fellow Anhui man. When he traced Chun's whereabouts, he learned the man had been dead for some time.

sentences.zh: 歸道呼圖壁，遇巡檢陳栻，亦皖人也，因跡椿，則死久矣。

translations.literal: Long said, "Chun's mother has waited day and night for her son's return—now that he is dead, what is to be done? Moreover, she sent the money with me because she believed I could deliver it; in conscience I cannot return the money empty-handed and leave Chun's bones unreturned. Yet the money is scant; even if I exhaust all in my purse, it is still not enough—what then?" He borrowed from Shi, took a roundabout route of eight thousand li, and brought Chun's coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: Long said, "Chun's mother has waited day and night for her son to come home—now he is dead. What can be done? She sent this money with me because she trusted I could deliver it. I cannot in good conscience return empty-handed and leave Chun's bones abroad. Yet the sum is too small; even if I emptied my purse it would not suffice—what then?" He borrowed from Shi, took an eight-thousand-li detour, and brought Chun's coffin home.

sentences.zh: 瓏曰：「椿母日夜望子歸，乃今死，當奈何？

translations.literal: Jiang Jian, courtesy name Feilin, was a native of Qianshan in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jian, styled Feilin, was from Qianshan in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 且以金附我者，為我能致之也，義不忍空返其金，令椿骨不還。

translations.literal: Even as a child he had keen judgment.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he showed sharp wit.

sentences.zh: 顧金少，盡吾橐中貲，猶不足，又當奈何？」

translations.literal: At age seven, following his uncle into a temple, he saw a county runner sitting in the corridor; he happened to speak with him and learned that a monk at a certain temple had been murdered without the culprit being found.
translations.idiomatic: At seven, entering a temple with his uncle, he saw a county runner seated in the corridor. Speaking with him by chance, he learned that a monk at a certain temple had been killed and the culprit could not be found.

sentences.zh: 貸於栻，迂道八千里，載椿柩以歸。

translations.literal: Jian told his uncle, "The killer is the old monk on the dais!" Even as he recited sutras he kept glancing about—his mind was not on the text. The runner led him away; one interrogation and he confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian told his uncle, "The murderer is the old monk on the dais!" Even while chanting sutras the monk kept looking about—his mind was not on the scripture. The runner hauled him off; one round of questioning and he confessed.

sentences.zh: 蔣堅，字非磷，江西鉛山人。

translations.literal: At seventeen, taking a boat past Ruihong, there was a youth on the same vessel who always went out to avoid meals; Jian grew suspicious and asked him.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, traveling by boat past Ruihong, he noticed a youth on the same vessel who always slipped away at mealtimes. Suspicious, Jian questioned him.

sentences.zh: 幼即有智數。

translations.literal: The youth said he was too poor to pay the boat fare and the boatmen would not feed him extra helpings, so he went out to avoid eating.
translations.idiomatic: The youth said he was too poor to pay his passage and the boatmen would give him no share of the food, so he stayed away at mealtimes.

sentences.zh: 七歲，從叔入寺，廡坐縣役，值與語，謂某寺僧被殺，不得其主名。

translations.literal: Jian invited him to eat together and gave him money. The man later died as a guest in a distant place; Jian also arranged to return his bones and the remaining money.
translations.idiomatic: Jian invited him to share his meal and gave him money. The man later died far from home; Jian also saw to it that his bones and the remaining money were returned.

sentences.zh: 堅語其叔曰：「殺人者，堂上老僧也！」

translations.literal: Growing up he studied Legalist doctrine, served on staff in Shanxi, and repeatedly cleared up doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he studied Legalist writings, served on staff in Shanxi, and repeatedly exonerated men in doubtful cases.

sentences.zh: 方誦經，屢顧，意乃不在經。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Kangxi, working under Tong Guolong, prefect of Zezhou, when the people of Linfen, driven to desperation by a corrupt clerk, rose in revolt, the governor dispatched Guolong to investigate; Jian followed Guolong with seven horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 52, serving under Tong Guolong, prefect of Zezhou, when the people of Linfen, pressed beyond endurance by a corrupt clerk, rose in revolt, the governor ordered Guolong to investigate. Jian accompanied him with seven mounted men.

sentences.zh: 役牽去，一訊而服。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the crowd at Baoshan was tumultuous; Jian used the governor's command arrow to address the people first.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival they found the crowd at Baoshan in uproar. Jian first addressed the people under the governor's command arrow.

sentences.zh: 年十七，附舟經瑞洪，有少年同舟，當食必出避，堅疑而問之。

translations.literal: Guolong entered the county seat, seized five or six clerks who had been harassing the people, flogged them until they bled; the crowd gathered to watch, and all clamor and uproar dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Guolong entered the county seat, seized five or six clerks who had been tormenting the people, and flogged them until they bled. The crowd gathered to watch, and the shouting and tumult melted away.

sentences.zh: 少年自言貧不能償舟值，舟人將不餘食焉，故出避。

translations.literal: Guolong requested retirement; Jian returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Guolong petitioned to retire; Jian went home.

sentences.zh: 堅邀與共食，資以金，其人後客死，又策返其骨及餘金。

translations.literal: Some years later, he heard that Guolong had been arrested and thrown into prison at Taiyuan because a subordinate had been short in the treasury accounts, and was required to make restitution of several thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he heard that Guolong had been arrested and imprisoned at Taiyuan because a subordinate's accounts were short, and that he was held liable for restitution of several thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 長習法家言，佐幕山西，屢雪疑獄。

translations.literal: Jian went to visit him, collected debts for Guolong in Luancheng, then went to Zezhou and borrowed from the people of the prefecture to pay Guolong's restitution; only then was the case resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Jian went to see him, collected debts on Guolong's behalf in Luancheng, then borrowed from the people of Zezhou to pay the restitution. Only then was the case cleared.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年，主澤州知州佟國瓏，臨汾民迫姦胥為變，巡撫檄國瓏往按，堅從國瓏以七騎往。

translations.literal: Jian once said, "Law exists to save the world; when the heart seeks to preserve human life, that is proper use of law."
translations.idiomatic: Jian once said, "Law exists to save the world. When the heart seeks to preserve life, that is the right way to use law."

sentences.zh: 至則眾保山洶洶，堅以巡撫令箭先諭眾。

translations.literal: He wrote the Qiushuji ("Collection on Seeking Life").
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Qiushuji, or Collection on Seeking Life.

sentences.zh: 國瓏入縣，執胥擾民者五六，笞之流血，眾就觀，歡譟悉散。

translations.literal: His son Shi Quan has a biography in the Wenyuans section.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi Quan is recorded in the Wenyuans section.

sentences.zh: 國瓏乞休，堅歸。

translations.literal: Li Linsun was a native of Xiangcheng in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linsun was from Xiangcheng in Henan.

sentences.zh: 數年，聞國瓏以屬吏虧帑逮下太原獄，責償數千金。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qianlong reign, sect rebels rose and were about to attack the provincial capital of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Qianlong years, sect rebels rose and prepared to attack the Henan provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 堅往省，為國瓏徵債欒城，又至澤州，貸於州民，為國瓏輸償，獄乃解。

translations.literal: At that time the provincial treasurer Ma Huiyu was in charge of the city's defense, but there were no troops and he saw no way to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial treasurer Ma Huiyu then held command of the city's defense, but he had no troops and saw no means of holding the rebels off.

sentences.zh: 堅嘗曰：「法所以救世，心求人之生，斯善用法矣。」

translations.literal: There was one Chen Boyu of Pixian, who had once been a client of the Henan governor; he had foretold that the sect rebels would rise and for this was imprisoned on charges of spreading heterodox talk.
translations.idiomatic: One Chen Boyu of Pixian had once served as a client of the Henan governor. He had warned beforehand that the sect rebels would rise and was jailed for spreading heterodox talk.

sentences.zh: 著求生集。

translations.literal: When disorders broke out in Sichuan and Hubei, the great officials treated him as an honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out in Sichuan and Hubei, the senior officials received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 子士銓，文苑有傳。

translations.literal: He befriended Linsun and spoke to Huiyu, having him lead five hundred local militiamen to help defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended Linsun and spoke to Huiyu, who then had Linsun lead five hundred local militiamen to help hold the city.

sentences.zh: 李林孫，河南襄城人。

translations.literal: When the sect rebels arrived, Boyu drilled two hundred fifty men facing the water in battle formation.
translations.idiomatic: When the sect rebels arrived, Boyu drilled two hundred and fifty men in battle formation facing the water.

sentences.zh: 乾隆末，教匪起，將攻河南會城。

translations.literal: The rebels, taking them lightly for their small numbers, drew near to watch; Linsun with two hundred fifty men came out from behind and struck from both sides, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, dismissing them for their small numbers, drew close to watch. Linsun then led two hundred and fifty men out from behind and struck from both flanks, shattering them completely.

sentences.zh: 是時布政使馬慧裕主城守，顧無兵，度無以御。

translations.literal: The magistrate Lin Lan begged his troops to garrison Lushi. The sect leader Zhang Chao'er came to attack, claiming a hundred thousand men; Lan had fewer than two thousand troops and none dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Lin Lan asked for troops to hold Lushi. The sect chieftain Zhang Chao'er came to attack at the head of what he claimed were a hundred thousand men. Lan had fewer than two thousand soldiers, and none dared advance.

sentences.zh: 有陳伯瑜者，郫縣人，嘗為河南巡撫客，先事言教匪且起，以妖言下獄。

translations.literal: There was one Chen Boyu, a man of Pixian, who had once been a client of the Henan governor; beforehand he had said the sect rebels would rise, and for this was imprisoned on charges of heterodox talk.
translations.idiomatic: One Chen Boyu of Pixian had once served as a client of the Henan governor. He had warned beforehand that the sect rebels would rise and was jailed for spreading heterodox talk.

sentences.zh: 川、楚亂作，諸大吏禮為上客。

translations.literal: When disorders broke out in Sichuan and Hubei, the great officials treated him as an honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out in Sichuan and Hubei, the senior officials received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 友林孫，言於慧裕，使率鄉兵五百人助守。

translations.literal: He befriended Li Linsun and spoke to Ma Huiyu, having him lead five hundred local militiamen to help defend.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended Li Linsun and spoke to Ma Huiyu, who then had Linsun lead five hundred local militiamen to help hold the city.

sentences.zh: 教匪至，伯瑜以二百五十人面水肄戰。

translations.literal: When the sect rebels arrived, Boyu drilled two hundred and fifty men facing the water in battle formation.
translations.idiomatic: When the sect rebels arrived, Boyu drilled two hundred and fifty men in battle formation facing the water.

sentences.zh: 匪易其少，就觀之，林孫以二百五十人出其背夾擊，大破之。

translations.literal: The rebels, taking them lightly for their small numbers, drew near to watch; Linsun with two hundred and fifty men came out from behind and struck from both sides, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, dismissing them for their small numbers, drew close to watch. Linsun then led two hundred and fifty men out from behind and struck from both flanks, shattering them completely.

sentences.zh: 知縣林嵐乞其兵守盧氏，教匪渠張潮兒來攻，號十萬，嵐兵不及二千，莫敢進。

translations.literal: Magistrate Lin Lan begged for his troops to garrison Lushi. The sect chieftain Zhang Chao'er came to attack, claiming a hundred thousand men; Lan's troops numbered fewer than two thousand, and none dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Lin Lan asked for troops to hold Lushi. The sect chieftain Zhang Chao'er came to attack at the head of what he claimed were a hundred thousand men. Lan had fewer than two thousand soldiers, and none dared advance.

sentences.zh: 嵐謝其眾曰：「公等皆林孫人，徒死無益。」

translations.literal: Lan addressed his troops, saying, "You are all men of Linsun's country; to die for nothing would serve no purpose."
translations.idiomatic: Lan spoke to his men: "You are all Linsun's countrymen. Pointless death gains nothing."

sentences.zh: 指大樹曰：「我官也，死是間耳。」

translations.literal: Pointing to a great tree, he said, "I am the magistrate; if I die, it shall be here between these branches."
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to a great tree. "I am the magistrate. If I die, let it be here beneath these branches."

sentences.zh: 眾怒曰：「誰無面目者，致公為此言？

translations.literal: The crowd angrily cried, "Who among us lacks face, that you should speak to us thus?
translations.idiomatic: The men flared up. "Who among us has no honor, that you should speak so?

sentences.zh: 今日戰，有不勝賊而生者，撞大石破腦死！」

translations.literal: Today we fight—whoever fails to defeat the bandits yet survives shall dash his head against the great stone and die!"
translations.idiomatic: Today we fight—any man who fails to beat the bandits yet lives shall smash his skull against that stone!"

sentences.zh: 嵐拜，眾亦拜。

translations.literal: Lan bowed, and the crowd bowed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Lan bowed; the men bowed in return.

sentences.zh: 遂戰，賊幾殲。

translations.literal: They then fought, and the bandits were nearly annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: They fought, and the bandits were nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 人或以兵家言問林孫，林孫謝不省，曰：「豪傑無他，得人心耳。」

translations.literal: Some questioned Linsun about military doctrine; Linsun begged off, saying he did not understand, and said, "Heroes have no other secret—they win men's hearts, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: When some questioned Linsun about military doctrine, he begged off, saying he knew nothing of such matters. "Heroes have no other art," he said. "They win men's hearts—that is all."

sentences.zh: 高大鎬，湖南桃源人。

translations.literal: Gao Dabao was a native of Taoyuan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dabao was from Taoyuan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父陛，臨淄知縣。

translations.literal: His father Bi had been magistrate of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bi had been magistrate of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，大鎬將僕王明省父歸，道荊門，遇教匪。

translations.literal: Early in the Jiaqing reign, Dabao was taking his servant Wang Ming home to visit his father; on the road at Jingmen they encountered sect rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing, Dabao was taking his servant Wang Ming home to see his father when, on the road at Jingmen, they ran into sect rebels.

sentences.zh: 大鎬從容語，使引見其渠。

translations.literal: Dabao spoke calmly and had them bring him before their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Dabao spoke with easy composure and had himself brought before the rebel chieftain.

sentences.zh: 渠疑為官軍諜，欲殺之。

translations.literal: The chieftain suspected he was a spy for the government army and wanted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain suspected him of being a government spy and meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 大鎬自言：「我盜也！

translations.literal: Dabao said of himself, "I am a bandit!
translations.idiomatic: Dabao declared, "I am a bandit myself!

sentences.zh: 奈何殺我？」

translations.literal: Why kill me?"
translations.idiomatic: Why kill me?"

sentences.zh: 渠使與其徒角，殺三人，乃錄與其徒伍。

translations.literal: The chieftain had him wrestle with his followers; he killed three men and was then enrolled among the band.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain had him fight his followers hand to hand. He killed three men and was taken into the band.

sentences.zh: 渠令攻宜城，大鎬從行，渡溪，匿橋下得脫。

translations.literal: The chieftain ordered an attack on Yicheng; Dabao went along, crossed a stream, hid beneath a bridge, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the chieftain ordered an attack on Yicheng, Dabao went along, but crossing a stream he hid beneath a bridge and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 遇餘寇，又殺三人，乃走宜城白吏，言寇且至，為畫城守策。

translations.literal: He met remaining bandits, killed three more men, then ran to Yicheng and reported to the officials that bandits were coming, and drew up a plan for defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: He met straggling bandits, killed three more, then hurried to Yicheng and warned the officials that raiders were coming, sketching out a plan for the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 大鎬在賊中久，知賊畏飛石，令盡發市衢街道民家階磩碎之，置城上。

translations.literal: Dabao had been long among the bandits and knew they feared flying stones; he ordered that all the step-stones of market lanes and street-front houses be broken up and placed atop the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Having lived long among the bandits, Dabao knew they feared hurled stones. He ordered the threshold stones of market lanes and street-front houses broken up and piled on the walls.

sentences.zh: 寇至，見有備乃走。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, they saw preparations had been made and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came and saw the city prepared, they turned away.

sentences.zh: 吏欲敘大鎬功，大鎬辭歸桃源。

translations.literal: The officials wished to record Dabao's merit, but Dabao declined and returned to Taoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The officials wanted to register Dabao's merit, but he refused and went home to Taoyuan.

sentences.zh: 王明在賊中，不與大鎬相聞，既為官兵所俘，讞非盜，釋之，亦得歸。

translations.literal: Wang Ming remained among the bandits with no word from Dabao; later he was captured by government troops, and since the case did not mark him as a bandit, he was released and also returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ming stayed among the bandits with no word from Dabao. Captured later by government troops, he was cleared of banditry and released, and he too made his way home.

sentences.zh: 許所望，字叔翹，安徽懷遠人。

translations.literal: Xu Suowang, courtesy name Shuqiao, was a native of Huaiyuan in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Suowang, styled Shuqiao, was from Huaiyuan in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate scholar.

sentences.zh: 工為詩。

translations.literal: He was skilled at composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in poetry.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年冬，宿州民王朝明、李勝才為亂，州破。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year of Jiaqing, the commoners Wang Chaoming and Li Shengca of Su Prefecture raised a revolt and the prefecture fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Jiaqing 7, Wang Chaoming and Li Shengca of Su Prefecture rebelled and the prefectural city fell.

sentences.zh: 所望與其戚王冠英出粟三千石佐軍，且率其徒邱惠齡、張國綱、謝崇訓等破賊陳家集。

translations.literal: Suowang and his kinsman Wang Guanying contributed three thousand shi of grain to aid the army, and also led his followers Qiu Huiling, Zhang Guogang, Xie Chongxun, and others to defeat the bandits at Chenjiaji.
translations.idiomatic: Suowang and his kinsman Wang Guanying contributed three thousand shi of grain to support the army, and Suowang led his followers Qiu Huiling, Zhang Guogang, Xie Chongxun, and others in breaking the bandits at Chenjiaji.

sentences.zh: 十八年秋，林清亂起，師圍滑縣，兩江總督百齡駐徐州，安徽巡撫胡克家駐亳州，為備。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighteenth year, the Lin Qing rebellion broke out; the army besieged Huaxian, Governor-General Bai Ling stationed himself at Xuzhou, and Anhui Governor Hu Kejia stationed himself at Bozhou in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Jiaqing 18 the Lin Qing rebellion erupted. Imperial forces besieged Huaxian; Governor-General Bai Ling took post at Xuzhou and Anhui Governor Hu Kejia at Bozhou to prepare.

sentences.zh: 歸德盜楊七郎據引河集，其黨洪廣漢據保安山，與潁州亂民沙占魁等遙相結，觀變。

translations.literal: The Guidé bandit Yang Qilang held Yinheji; his follower Hong Guanghan held Bao'an Mountain; they joined forces from afar with the disorderly men of Yingzhou such as Sha Zhankui and watched how events would turn.
translations.idiomatic: The Guidé bandit Yang Qilang held Yinheji, his lieutenant Hong Guanghan held Bao'an Mountain, and they kept in distant contact with Yingzhou rebels such as Sha Zhankui, waiting to see which way fortune would turn.

sentences.zh: 克家知所望，以書招之。

translations.literal: Kejia knew Suowang and summoned him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: Kejia knew Suowang's reputation and summoned him by letter.

sentences.zh: 所望率八百人至亳州，以惠齡等十人為隊長。

translations.literal: Suowang led eight hundred men to Bozhou and made Huiling and nine others squad leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Suowang led eight hundred men to Bozhou and appointed Huiling and nine others as squad captains.

sentences.zh: 所望謀曰：「楊七郎猛且狡，宜以計誘之。」

translations.literal: Suowang planned, saying: "Yang Qilang is fierce and cunning; he should be lured by stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Suowang said, "Yang Qilang is fierce and cunning—we must draw him out by guile."

sentences.zh: 令國綱、崇訓率健兒八人偽為逃卒詣七郎，越五日誘之出，以百餘人至邱家集。

translations.literal: He had Guogang and Chongxun lead eight stalwart men disguised as deserters to Qilang; after five days they lured him out, and he came with a little over a hundred men to Qiujiaji.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Guogang and Chongxun with eight picked men disguised as deserters to Qilang. Five days later they enticed him out with a little over a hundred men to Qiujiaji.

sentences.zh: 七郎忽疑曰：「若為許所望來耶？」

translations.literal: Qilang suddenly grew suspicious and said: "Have you come on Xu Suowang's orders?"
translations.idiomatic: Qilang suddenly suspected them. "Have you come for Xu Suowang?"

sentences.zh: 崇訓出不意斷七郎臂，眾大驚，國綱疾呼曰：「我張國綱也！」

translations.literal: Chongxun unexpectedly severed Qilang's arm; the band panicked, and Guogang shouted at once: "I am Zhang Guogang!"
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun struck without warning and severed Qilang's arm. The bandits panicked. Guogang shouted, "I am Zhang Guogang!"

sentences.zh: 立擊殺數人、國綱與惠齡同破宿州賊，以勇聞，賊素憚之，遂大潰。

translations.literal: He immediately struck down several men. Guogang and Huiling had earlier broken the Suzhou bandits and were famed for courage; the bandits had long feared them, and now they broke and fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He cut down several men at once. Guogang and Huiling had crushed the Suzhou rebels and were known for valor; the bandits had long feared them and now fled in complete rout.

sentences.zh: 所望率兵至，七郎走死，廣漢亦潰。

translations.literal: Suowang led his troops up; Qilang fled to his death, and Guanghan's force also broke.
translations.idiomatic: Suowang brought up his troops. Qilang fled to his death and Guanghan's force collapsed.

sentences.zh: 占魁等走永城，會師克滑縣，餘賊走與合，焚會亭。

translations.literal: Zhankui and the others fled to Yongcheng. When the main army took Huaxian, the remaining bandits fled to join them and burned Huiting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhankui and the others retreated toward Yongcheng. When the main army captured Huaxian, surviving bandits fled to join them and burned Huiting.

sentences.zh: 所望與戰公基湖，列十火槍土埠上，令眾伏地，曰：「賊至二百步，槍發，乘煙疾進擊之。」

translations.literal: Suowang fought at Gongjihu, lined ten fire-guns on an earthen mound, ordered the men to lie flat, and said: "When the bandits reach two hundred paces, fire the guns and charge swiftly through the smoke."
translations.idiomatic: At Gongjihu Suowang drew up ten fire-guns on an earthen mound and had his men lie flat. "When the bandits come within two hundred paces," he said, "fire, then charge through the smoke."

sentences.zh: 賊潰奔，逐之數十里，亳州師乃罷。

translations.literal: The bandits broke and fled; they were pursued for several tens of li, and only then did the Bozhou force stand down.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits broke and ran. Pursued for miles, they were not finally dispersed until the Bozhou force stood down.

sentences.zh: 百齡在徐州，亦得河南張永祥者，以鄉兵三百助守。

translations.literal: Bai Ling, at Xuzhou, also obtained Zhang Yongxiang of Henan, who helped defend with three hundred local militiamen.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou Bai Ling also enlisted Zhang Yongxiang of Henan, who helped hold the line with three hundred local militiamen.

sentences.zh: 事定，所望辭敘功，以諸生應試如故。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Suowang declined credit for merit and returned to his licentiate examinations as before.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, Suowang refused any record of merit and went back to his examinations as a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 永祥從巡撫阮元自河南移浙江，亦罷去，人呼為張鐵槍雲。

translations.literal: Yongxiang followed Governor Ruan Yuan from Henan to Zhejiang and then withdrew; people called him Iron-Spear Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxiang followed Governor Ruan Yuan from Henan to Zhejiang and then retired; men called him Iron-Spear Zhang.

sentences.zh: 邢清源，曹州人。

translations.literal: Xing Qingyuan was a native of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Qingyuan was from Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 入鎮標為兵數十年，老而退伍。

translations.literal: He entered the garrison banner as a soldier and served for decades, retiring in old age.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted in the garrison banner and served as a soldier for decades before retiring in old age.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，長槍會為亂，圍曹州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng the Long Spear Society rebelled and besieged Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 11 the Long Spear Society rose in rebellion and besieged Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 時親王僧格林沁駐軍濟寧，欲乞援，無敢齎書往者，清源請行。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Sengge Rinchen was encamped at Jining; they wished to beg for relief, but no one dared carry a letter; Qingyuan volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sengge Rinchen was then encamped at Jining. The city needed relief, yet no one dared carry a message through the siege. Qingyuan offered to go.

sentences.zh: 乃裂帛為牘，置清源衣帶，清源破衣持竹杖為丐者狀，出圍達王所。

translations.literal: They tore silk into a dispatch and hid it in Qingyuan's belt; Qingyuan, in ragged clothes with a bamboo staff in the guise of a beggar, broke through the siege and reached the prince.
translations.idiomatic: They tore silk into a dispatch and hid it in Qingyuan's belt. Dressed in rags and leaning on a bamboo staff like a beggar, Qingyuan broke through the siege and reached the prince.

sentences.zh: 王即札示發兵狀，仍置衣帶還報，兵至，城得全。

translations.literal: The prince at once issued orders to dispatch troops, again hid the dispatch in his belt for the return report, and when the troops arrived the city was saved.
translations.idiomatic: The prince immediately issued orders to march; the dispatch was hidden in his belt again for the return journey. When the relief force arrived, the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 王元，杭州旗營牧馬人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yuan was a groom of the Hangzhou banner garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan was a groom in the Hangzhou banner garrison.

sentences.zh: 粵寇陷省城，將軍瑞昌守旗營，令元持書突圍出乞援張玉良，大哭不食。

translations.literal: When the Cantonese rebels took the provincial city, General Ruichang held the banner camp and ordered Yuan to break through the siege with a letter begging Zhang Yuliang for relief; Yuan wept and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cantonese rebels took the provincial capital, General Ruichang held the banner camp and sent Yuan through the siege with a letter pleading for Zhang Yuliang's relief. Yuan wept and refused food.

sentences.zh: 玉良義之，立進兵。

translations.literal: Yuliang honored his righteousness and advanced at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang was moved by his loyalty and marched at once.

sentences.zh: 瑞昌夾擊，遂復省城。

translations.literal: Ruichang struck from both sides and recovered the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Ruichang attacked from both sides and retook the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，城再陷，元已保營官，戰歿長安，附祀瑞昌祠。

translations.literal: The next year the city fell again; Yuan had already been promoted to camp officer and died in battle at Chang'an, receiving posthumous sacrifice in Ruichang's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the city fell again. Yuan, by then a camp officer, was killed fighting at Chang'an and was honored with sacrifice in Ruichang's shrine.

sentences.zh: 鳳瑞，字桐山，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正白旗人，乍浦駐防。

translations.literal: Feng Rui, courtesy name Tongshan, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner, garrisoned at Zhapu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Rui, styled Tongshan, belonged to the Guwalgiya clan—a Manchu of the Plain White Banner stationed at Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 粵寇來犯，與兄麟瑞戰禦。

translations.literal: When Cantonese rebels came to attack, he fought to defend together with his elder brother Linrui.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping rebels struck, he and his elder brother Linrui fought to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 城陷，麟瑞陣歿，見忠義傳。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Linrui died on the battlefield; see the Biographies of the Faithful and Righteous.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell; Linrui died in battle. His account appears among the Biographies of the Faithful and Righteous.

sentences.zh: 鳳瑞改隸李鴻章軍，轉戰江、浙，屢有功，而太倉一役尤著。

translations.literal: Feng Rui then transferred to Li Hongzhang's army, campaigning through Jiangsu and Zhejiang with repeated merit, especially distinguished at the battle of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Rui then entered Li Hongzhang's service and campaigned across Jiangsu and Zhejiang with repeated distinction, above all at Taicang.

sentences.zh: 初，李軍以乏餉不用命，鳳瑞力保盜魁賀國賢，國賢本鹽商，官誣殺其兄，乃為盜。

translations.literal: At first Li's army, for lack of pay, would not obey orders; Feng Rui strongly vouched for the bandit chieftain He Guoxian. Guoxian had originally been a salt merchant; officials had falsely killed his elder brother, whereupon he became a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li's troops, unpaid, refused to fight. Feng Rui stood up for the bandit leader He Guoxian—a salt merchant whose brother officials had murdered on false charges, driving him to the hills.

sentences.zh: 鳳瑞與其兄善，責以大義，立出十萬金助餉，並率所部奮攻城，遂克太倉州。

translations.literal: Feng Rui was on good terms with him, admonished him with the greater right, at once furnished a hundred thousand in gold to aid the pay chest, and also led his command in a fierce assault on the city, thus capturing Taicang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Close to Guoxian, Feng Rui appealed to his sense of duty. Guoxian immediately pledged a hundred thousand in gold for the army's pay and led his men in a furious assault that took Taicang.

sentences.zh: 國賢後官至總兵，鳳瑞以筆帖式積功累保副都統，賞花翎。

translations.literal: Guoxian later rose to regional commander; Feng Rui, starting as a clerk, accumulated merit and was repeatedly promoted to vice commander-in-chief, and was awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxian later became a regional commander. Feng Rui, beginning as a clerk, rose by merit to vice commander-in-chief and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 江南平，調歸杭州，遂隱居不仕。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified he was transferred back to Hangzhou and then lived in retirement without taking office.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan was pacified he returned to Hangzhou and withdrew from public life.

sentences.zh: 時難民遍地，鳳瑞先於上海、青浦設廠施衣食，為謀棲宿，分遣歸里。

translations.literal: Refugees then covered the land; Feng Rui first set up relief stations at Shanghai and Qingpu to give food and clothing, find them shelter, and send them home by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees then filled the land. Feng Rui opened relief stations at Shanghai and Qingpu, giving food and clothing, finding shelter, and sending people home in turn.

sentences.zh: 复奉詔招集旗人歸防安插，恢復營製。

translations.literal: He also received an edict to gather banner people back to garrison duty, settle them, and restore camp organization.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he also gathered banner people back to garrison duty, resettled them, and restored the old camp system.

sentences.zh: 建昭忠祠，立忠義墳。

translations.literal: He built the Zhaozhong Shrine and established a tomb for the faithful and righteous.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Zhaozhong Shrine and raised a tomb for the faithful and righteous.

sentences.zh: 凡杭、乍兩營死者逾萬人，屍骨狼藉，躬督檢埋，分建兩大塚於兩地。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand men of the Hangzhou and Zhapu garrisons had died; bones lay scattered everywhere, and he personally supervised their collection and burial, raising two great burial mounds in the two places.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand men of the Hangzhou and Zhapu garrisons had fallen; bones lay scattered, and he personally oversaw their collection and burial, raising two great mounds in the two places.

sentences.zh: 勒碑致祭，列入祀典。

translations.literal: He carved steles and performed sacrifices, and had them entered in the state cult.
translations.idiomatic: He set up steles and sacrifices and had them entered in the state cult.

sentences.zh: 又採訪姓名，匯刻浙江八旗殉難錄。

translations.literal: He also gathered names and compiled and printed the Record of Zhejiang Eight Banners Martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: He also collected names and compiled the Record of Zhejiang Banner Martyrs.

sentences.zh: 乍浦副都統錫齡阿全家同殉，其僕石某獨負其幼子出，乞食養之。

translations.literal: The Zhapu vice commander-in-chief Xiling'a's entire household died together; only his servant, a man surnamed Shi, carried his young son out and begged for food to raise him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhapu vice commander Xiling'a's whole household perished together. Only his servant, a man surnamed Shi, carried out the young son and begged to keep him alive.

sentences.zh: 鳳瑞見而言於巡撫薛煥，奏請撫卹，為賦義僕行，給貲送歸。

translations.literal: Feng Rui saw this and spoke to Governor Xue Huan; a memorial was submitted for relief, a Ballad of the Righteous Servant was composed, and funds were given to send the boy home.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Rui saw this and spoke to Governor Xue Huan. A memorial was submitted for relief, a poem was written in praise of the faithful servant, and funds were provided to send the boy home.

sentences.zh: 鳳瑞義俠，好行善，歲收租穀數百石，必盡散之窮乏，數十年如一日，眾稱善人。

translations.literal: Feng Rui was righteous and chivalrous, fond of doing good; each year he received several hundred shi of rent grain and always gave it all to the destitute, decade after decade without change, and the people called him a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous and chivalrous, Feng Rui loved to do good. Each year he received several hundred shi of rent grain and gave every measure to the poor, decade after decade without fail. The people called him a good man.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十有二，贈將軍。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-two and was posthumously granted the rank of general.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-two and was posthumously made a general.

sentences.zh: 鳳瑞博學，工書畫，遊跡遍天下，嘗自刊玉章，曰「讀萬卷書，行萬里路。」

translations.literal: Feng Rui was broadly learned and skilled in calligraphy and painting; his travels took him everywhere under heaven. He once carved a jade seal reading, "Read ten thousand volumes; travel ten thousand li."
