translations.idiomatic: Feng Rui was widely learned and accomplished in calligraphy and painting; his travels carried him across the empire. He once carved a jade seal with the words, "Read ten thousand books; walk ten thousand li."

sentences.zh: 著有老子解、如如老人詩草及殉難錄等。

translations.literal: He wrote such works as Exposition of the Laozi, the Poetry Drafts of the Old Man Ruru, and the Martyrs' Record.
translations.idiomatic: Among his writings are Exposition of the Laozi, the Poetry Drafts of the Old Man Ruru, and the Martyrs' Record.

sentences.zh: 子四，文梁年十三，母病危，剖心以救，母愈，文梁竟卒。

translations.literal: He had four sons. Wenliang, at thirteen, when his mother lay critically ill, cut open his chest to save her; his mother recovered, but Wenliang died.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons. Wenliang, at thirteen, when his mother lay near death, cut open his own chest to save her. She recovered; Wenliang did not.

sentences.zh: 方元衡，字莘田，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Fang Yuanheng, courtesy name Xintian, was a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yuanheng, styled Xintian, was from Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 以貢生官光祿寺署正。

translations.literal: As a tribute student he served as acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Through tribute-student status he served as acting director at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 父病失明，晨夕調護，廁牏必躬親之，終親之身不稍怠。

translations.literal: When his father fell ill and lost his sight, he nursed him morning and evening; he always attended the privy himself and never slackened while his father lived.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill and went blind, he tended him morning and night, always attending the privy himself, and never slackened so long as his father lived.

sentences.zh: 推產給弟，惟筆耕以奉甘旨。

translations.literal: He gave his property to his younger brother and supported his parents on nothing but his pen.
translations.idiomatic: He turned his estate over to his younger brother and supported his parents solely by his writing.

sentences.zh: 年五十，依母懷如嬰兒。

translations.literal: At fifty he clung to his mother as an infant clings to the breast.
translations.idiomatic: At fifty he still clung to his mother like an infant in her arms.

sentences.zh: 居喪不宴笑，不居內，日所行必告於主，葬則廬墓側，歲時祭，必哀戚盡禮。

translations.literal: During mourning he neither feasted nor laughed, nor stayed in the inner quarters; each day's actions he reported to the spirit tablet, and at burial he lodged beside the tomb; at seasonal sacrifices he observed every rite in full grief.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he neither feasted nor laughed, nor slept in the inner rooms. Each day's doings he reported to the spirit tablet. At burial he lodged beside the tomb, and at seasonal rites he mourned with full propriety.

sentences.zh: 俗惑於風水，常停柩久不葬，請設勸葬局，限期督葬，無後者則購地代葬之，先後逾五萬俱。

translations.literal: The people, deluded by geomancy, often kept coffins long unburied; he petitioned to establish an Encouragement of Burial Bureau, set deadlines and supervised burial, and for those without heirs bought land and buried them on their behalf—more than fifty thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Deluded by geomancy, people often left coffins unburied for years. He petitioned to establish an Encouragement of Burial Bureau, set deadlines, and supervised burials; where there were no heirs he bought land and buried the dead himself—more than fifty thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 復設採訪局，採訪全省節孝貞烈，歷二十年，匯請得旌者凡十餘萬人。

translations.literal: He also established an Inquiry Bureau to investigate chaste and faithful women throughout the province; over twenty years the petitions submitted and honors granted totaled more than a hundred thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened an Inquiry Bureau to gather cases of chaste and faithful women across the province. Over twenty years the honors petitioned and granted came to more than a hundred thousand persons.

sentences.zh: 建總祠總坊於省會，有司春秋致祭。

translations.literal: He built a general shrine and memorial arch at the provincial capital, and the officials performed spring and autumn sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He built a general shrine and memorial arch at the provincial capital, where officials performed sacrifices in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 著有續心學宗、孝經淺註。

translations.literal: He wrote Continuation of the Heart Learning Tradition and Brief Commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include Continuation of the Heart Learning Tradition and Brief Commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 卒後，皖人上其孝義行，特贈五品卿。

translations.literal: After his death the people of Anhui submitted an account of his filial and righteous conduct, and he was specially granted the rank of fifth-grade dignitary.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the people of Anhui memorialized his filial and righteous conduct, and he was specially granted fifth-grade dignitary rank.

sentences.zh: 武訓，山東堂邑人。

translations.literal: Wu Xun was a native of Tangyi in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xun came from Tangyi in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 乞者也，初無名，以其第曰武七。

translations.literal: He was a beggar; at first he had no given name and was called Wu Seven from his place in the family.
translations.idiomatic: He was a beggar. At first he had no proper name and was known as Wu Seven from his birth order.

sentences.zh: 七孤貧，從母乞於市，得錢必市甘旨奉母。

translations.literal: Seven was orphaned and poor; he begged with his mother in the market, and whatever money he got he always bought delicacies to serve his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and destitute, Seven begged with his mother in the market. Whatever coin he earned he spent on delicacies for her.

sentences.zh: 母既喪，稍長，且傭且乞。

translations.literal: After his mother died he grew somewhat older and both hired himself out and begged.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he grew a little older and both hired himself out and begged.

sentences.zh: 自恨不識字，誓積貲設義學，以所得錢寄富家權子母，積三十人，得田二百三十畝有奇，乞如故。

translations.literal: He regretted that he could not read and vowed to save money to establish a charity school; he deposited his earnings with wealthy families at interest, and when thirty such depositors had been gathered he obtained more than two hundred thirty mu of land, while begging as before.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed that he could not read, he vowed to save for a charity school. He lent his earnings to wealthy families at interest; when thirty lenders had joined him he held more than two hundred thirty mu of land—and still begged as before.

sentences.zh: 藍縷蔽骭，晝乞而夜織。

translations.literal: In ragged clothes that barely covered his shins, he begged by day and wove by night.
translations.idiomatic: Clad in tatters that barely covered his shins, he begged by day and wove by night.

sentences.zh: 或勸其娶，七謝之。

translations.literal: Some urged him to marry; Seven declined.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to marry. Seven refused.

sentences.zh: 又數年，設義塾柳林莊，築塾費錢四千餘緡，盡出所積田以資塾。

translations.literal: Several years later he established a charity school at Liulin Village; building the school cost more than four thousand strings of cash, and he gave all the land he had accumulated to support it.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he opened a charity school at Liulin Village. Building it cost more than four thousand strings of cash, and he gave all his accumulated land to sustain it.

sentences.zh: 塾為二級，曰蒙學，曰經學。

translations.literal: The school had two levels, called Elementary Study and Classic Study.
translations.idiomatic: The school had two levels: Elementary Study and Classic Study.

sentences.zh: 開塾日，七先拜塾師，次遍拜諸生，具盛饌饗師，七屏立門外，俟宴罷，啜其餘。

translations.literal: On the day the school opened, Seven first bowed to the schoolmaster, then bowed in turn to all the students; a feast was prepared for the master, and Seven stood aside outside the gate, waiting until the banquet was over to sip what remained.
translations.idiomatic: On opening day Seven first bowed to the schoolmaster, then to every pupil. A feast was laid for the master; Seven stood outside the gate and, when the banquet ended, drank what was left.

sentences.zh: 曰：「我乞者，不敢與師抗禮也！」

translations.literal: He said: "I am a beggar—I dare not return the master's courtesy as an equal!"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I am a beggar. I dare not stand on equal footing with my teacher!"

sentences.zh: 常往來塾中，值師晝寢，默跪榻前，師覺驚起；

translations.literal: He often came and went in the school; when he found the master napping by day he silently knelt before the couch, and when the master woke he started up in alarm;
translations.idiomatic: He was often at the school. If he found the master napping by day he knelt silently before the couch until the master woke with a start;

sentences.zh: 遇學生遊戲，亦如之：師生相戒勉。

translations.literal: when he met students at play he did the same: master and pupils admonished one another.
translations.idiomatic: when he saw pupils at play he did the same, and master and students admonished one another.

sentences.zh: 於學有不謹者，七聞之，泣且勸。

translations.literal: When someone in the school was remiss, Seven heard of it and wept as he admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: When a pupil was careless, Seven wept as he urged him on.

sentences.zh: 有司旌其勤，名之曰訓。

translations.literal: The authorities commended his diligence and named him Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities commended his devotion and gave him the name Xun.

sentences.zh: 嘗至館陶，僧了證設塾鴉莊，貲不足，出錢數百緡助其成。

translations.literal: Once he went to Guantao; the monk Liaozheng was setting up a school at Yazhuang but lacked funds, and he contributed several hundred strings of cash to help complete it.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Guantao he found the monk Liaozheng opening a school at Yazhuang but short of funds; he gave several hundred strings of cash to finish it.

sentences.zh: 复積金千餘，建義塾臨清，皆以其姓名名焉。

translations.literal: He also accumulated more than a thousand in gold and built charity schools at Linqing, each named after himself.
translations.idiomatic: He saved more than a thousand taels and built charity schools at Linqing, each bearing his name.

sentences.zh: 縣有嫠張陳氏，家貧，刲肉以奉姑，訓予田十畝助其養。

translations.literal: In the county was a widow, Lady Zhang of the Chen clan, poor, who cut flesh from her own body to serve her mother-in-law; Xun gave her ten mu of field to aid her support.
translations.idiomatic: In the county lived a poor widow, Lady Zhang of the Chen clan, who cut her own flesh to feed her mother-in-law. Xun gave her ten mu of land to help her.

sentences.zh: 遇孤寒，輒假以錢，終身不取，亦不以告人。

translations.literal: When he met the orphaned and destitute he lent them money, never collected it in his lifetime, and never told others.
translations.idiomatic: To the orphaned and destitute he lent money he never collected in life, and never spoke of it to anyone.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十二年，歿臨清義塾廡下，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Guangxu he died beneath the corridor of the Linqing charity school, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 22 he died under the eaves of the Linqing charity school, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 病革，聞諸生誦讀聲，猶張目而笑。

translations.literal: Near death, when he heard the students' recitation he still opened his eyes and smiled.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed, hearing pupils recite their lessons, he still opened his eyes and smiled.

sentences.zh: 縣人感其義，鐫像於石，歸田四十畝，以其從子奉祀。

translations.literal: The people of the county, moved by his righteousness, carved his image in stone, restored forty mu of land, and had his nephew perform the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The county, moved by his example, carved his likeness in stone, restored forty mu of land, and appointed his nephew to tend his rites.

sentences.zh: 山東巡撫張曜、袁樹勳先後疏請旌，祀孝義祠。

translations.literal: The Shandong governors Zhang Yao and Yuan Shuxun memorialized in succession for official commendation, and he was enshrined in the Shrine of Filial Piety and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Governors Zhang Yao and Yuan Shuxun of Shandong memorialized in turn for his commendation, and he was enshrined in the Shrine of Filial Piety and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 呂聯珠，字星五，漢軍正黃旗人，隸盛京內務府。

translations.literal: Lü Lianzhu, courtesy name Xingwu, a Han bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner, attached to the Inner Palace Office of Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Lianzhu, styled Xingwu, was a Han bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner serving in the Mukden Inner Palace Office.

sentences.zh: 所居村曰瓦子峪。

translations.literal: The village where he lived was called Waziyu.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a village called Waziyu.

sentences.zh: 貧，授徒為大父及父母養，一介不妄取。

translations.literal: Poor, he taught pupils to support his grandfather and parents, and never took so much as a speck unearned.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he taught to support his grandfather and parents and never accepted so much as a grain he had not earned.

sentences.zh: 應鄉試，徒步千餘裡，有富家子招與同乘，堅卻之。

translations.literal: When he went up for the provincial examination he walked more than a thousand li; a rich man's son invited him to ride together and he firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Going up for the provincial examination he walked more than a thousand li. A rich man's son offered him a seat in his carriage; he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 光緒十四年，舉於鄉，授筆帖式，補催長，不改其狷。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Guangxu he passed the provincial examination, was appointed a clerk, and filled the post of revenue collector, yet did not change his upright scruples.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 14 he passed the provincial examination, became a clerk, and served as revenue collector without softening his strict integrity.

sentences.zh: 聯珠有從叔，其一貧，無子，請兼祧侍養。

translations.literal: Lianzhu had two younger uncles on his father's side; one was poor and childless, and asked to be served through joint adoption.
translations.idiomatic: Lianzhu had two paternal cousins once removed. One was poor and childless and asked to be kept through joint adoption.

sentences.zh: 叔嚴急，事之盡禮；

translations.literal: The uncle was stern and exacting, yet he served him with full propriety;
translations.idiomatic: That uncle was harsh and demanding, yet he served him with full propriety;

sentences.zh: 其一出遠遊，以廢疾歸，奉於家，喪葬婚嫁力任之。

translations.literal: the other went far away to travel, returned crippled by illness, and Lianzhu kept him at home, bearing the full burden of funeral, marriage, and other obligations.
translations.idiomatic: the other had gone far abroad, returned broken by illness, and Lianzhu kept him at home, shouldering funeral, marriage, and every other duty.

sentences.zh: 有田招佃以耕，鄰田鬻於人，佔聯珠田五尺，聯珠言於官，讓與之。

translations.literal: He had fields that he leased out for farming; when a neighbor sold land to someone who encroached five chi on Lianzhu's fields, Lianzhu reported it to the magistrate and yielded the encroached portion.
translations.idiomatic: He leased out his fields. When a neighbor's buyer encroached five chi on his land, Lianzhu reported it to the magistrate and yielded the strip.

sentences.zh: 田中有他氏墓，為之掃除歲祭焉。

translations.literal: In his fields was another family's tomb, and he swept and maintained it with annual sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Another family's tomb stood in his fields; he swept it and made offerings every year.

sentences.zh: 同學坐事繫獄死，為之葬。

translations.literal: A fellow student was imprisoned for an offense and died; he buried him.
translations.idiomatic: A classmate imprisoned on a charge died in custody; Lianzhu buried him.

sentences.zh: 姻家有以疑獄死京師者，赴會試，為攜其骨還葬。

translations.literal: A relative by marriage had died in a doubtful case in the capital; when Lianzhu went for the metropolitan examination he carried the bones home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman by marriage had died in a disputed case in the capital; on his way to the metropolitan examination Lianzhu carried the bones home for burial.

sentences.zh: 聯珠篤行，式於鄉人。

translations.literal: Lianzhu was upright in conduct and served as a model to the people of his village.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply upright, Lianzhu set the standard for his neighbors.

sentences.zh: 治程、硃之學，鄉人奉其教。

translations.literal: He studied the learning of Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, and the villagers followed his teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the learning of Cheng and Zhu, and the village looked to his instruction.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died.
